The Basilisk is a unique vehicle in the world of Cyberpunk 2077. Compared to other vehicles, the Basilisk has:
No visible suspension when using jet rockets for lift,
Full-range multi-directional movement,
Rotational movement while stationary,
Combat capabilities (some models)
Unque piloting experience,
Unique command input, whereby it's possible to pilot and use combat systems simultaneously in armed models.

The Basilisk is equipped with smart missiles that home in on your target. Press <Input context="VehicleTankDrive" actionName="ShootSecondary" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to fire a homing missile to attack your selected target.

Panzer's movement is completely unique and is more reliant on player movement than standard road vehicles. Instead of using gas and brake pedals, the Basilisk uses biometric thumb data for movement. Use [Left Joystick] to maneuver the Panzer.

The primary cannon can rotate 360 degrees and has two modes of fire:\n1) Standard automatic fire. The double-barrels alternate fire as long as the trigger is pressed. Press [R2] to enter the mode and hold it to sustain fire.\n2) Precision strikes. Hold [L2] to enter this mode. Holding [L2] allows you to fire both barrels simultaneously. This mode provides greater precision and less dispersion, but reduces the rate of fire.
Access your phone with <Input actionName="OpenPhone" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.
During this job, you will have your netrunner, T-Bug, on the phone to help guide you through its different stages.
Objects highlighted in yellow contain valuable tips to help you with the current job.
To quickhack a camera, you must first scan it using your optical cyberware. This gives you several options such as taking control of the camera, shifting its field of vision or shutting it down.

Scanning a device with your optical cyberware will display useful information about its capabilities and vulnerabilities.

Devices that have a vulnerability are illuminated with a special highlight.

Look at a device and press <Input actionName="InteractionWheelScan" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to enter quickhacking mode.

Then, select a vulnerability from the list and press <Input actionName="UI_Apply" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

Select the quickhack from the quick-access menu. If you don't have the necessary Skill level, the option will be unusable and grayed out. For this task, T-Bug gave you a special shard that imitates a cyberdeck.
You can buy cyberware and upgrades at ripperdoc clinics. To buy a piece of cyberware, select it from the list. Then, if you have enough money to buy it, the ripperdoc will install it for you.

Patience is a virtue. Typically, when you finish talking with another character, they will return to their interrupted activities, giving you an opportunity to act. Some conversations also serve as a source of useful hints about the location or about your current objectives.
Press and hold <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to use the scanner.
Using your optical cyberware, you can scan objects, enemies and other people to reveal additional information about them.
Shoot at the targets to score points. Try this out if you want to test weapon or just feel like unwinding.
As you level up your Attributes, you may unlock new interactions with the environment that allow you to take different approaches when completing Jobs and Gigs.

Your Stash is secure system to store equipment and can be accessed from all of your available safehouses and vehicles. For example, if you store something in your car trunk, you'll be able to access it from your apartment later on.\n\nLegendary weapons stored in your Stash will appear on the trophy wall in your apartment.
You can earn Street Cred by bumping into new people and helping them solve their problems. So get out there and look for all kinds of opportunities!

Gigs are tasks offered by fixers in each of Night City's districts. When you enter a district, you will receive a text message from the local fixer that details all of the available Gigs, automatically marking their locations on your map. When you approach a Gig location closely enough, you will receive another text message with a task brief and your Journal will update with the information.

Cyberpunk 2077 can be completed with a non-lethal, stealth-based playstyle. You never have to kill a single person if you don't want to.

Keep in mind that enemies will be alerted to your presence if you make too much noise. Running, jumping and shooting will cause enemies to investigate the source of the noise.

When an enemy detects you, an Alert Indicator will appear above their head. To prevent the indicator from filling up, either deal with the enemy silently or hide.

You can "defeat" an enemy by killing them or by downing them non-lethally with ranged attacks, melee attacks and takedowns. When you down an enemy non-lethally, they become incapacitated, allowing you to move their body, hide it or search it for loot. It's your choice to finish them off with a killing blow or not. But be aware: dealing a high amount of damage at once or performing a lethal takedown will kill them instantly. Consider your moves carefully.
Your acquaintances can send text messages, which can be read at any time on your phone. To close a message, press <Input actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Look out for objects than can be scanned with your optical cyberware. If a device can be hacked and used to enter the network, it is called a Weak Point. To use it, scan it by pressing <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

What's up, BD-maniacs? Hungry for a new emo-rush? Then check out the latest word from the freshest BDs on the market.

Foreign Body
The body is everything. There is nothing else. It is you, but it is also just a tool for your mind to interact with the world. But what would happen if this tool tried to live its own life? What if it tried... to kill you?
Though not a particularly original addition to the thriller genre, this braindance featuring Luke Poller is still a solid experiential ride. The fear of disobedient implants has been around since pirates were walking around on peg legs – well, maybe not that long – as a result, the trope has been pervasive in film, braindance, and urban legend alike. Still, "Foreign Body" borrows some of the genre's best elements while still incorporating just enough new stuff to the mix to keep it interesting. After all, it's not every day you see the world from the perspective of a sentient arm.

Maxwell's Rehab
This braindance season has been chock full of horror, but this one stands out from the rest. The always phenomenal Maxwell Ramirez is pushed to the brink of cyberpsychosis so we can relive his return to normalcy. The title offers a tone of optimism, but don't let that fool you. You will relive Maxwell's slip into psychosis, the heartbreak of his wife, and the gradual reintegration into a world that is now far different from how he left it. This BD is a must-relive of the season, but it's not for the faint of heart.

Badlands Raid
At last, a BD for those looking for something a little lighter. "Badlands Raid" is a remake of the 2023 classic, which was an innovative tour de force of the time. For those of you unfamiliar, the plot revolves around an ordinary, boring guy who accidentally gets tangled up in a nomad ambush on a Zetatech convoy. I won't spoil it because, even though the main plot hasn't changed in 54 years, most people these days probably don't know the ending. What I will say is this: the remake's creators have introduced a few modern twists into the story that should make for a pleasant surprise to classics-lovers and newbies alike.

Interviewer: For most of us, the precepts of Buddhism seem baffling to say the least. How would you explain to the average Night Citizen why bhikkhu such as yourself are against implanting cybernetic technology into their bodies?

Monk: It's not that we're against them, per say. Every person has the right to make choices with their body so long as those choices don't harm another. Though bhikkhu do abide by stricter rules, such as abstaining from cyberware, in order to achieve Enlightenment.

Interviewer: Then what does your hesitation stem from? How do cybernetics affect your pursuit of Enlightenment?

Monk: Well...(short pause) Among other things, it's their vague, fluid status... for lack of a better word. Ask yourself – what is an implant? A part of your body? An impersonal object?

Interviewer: You're asking me? Uh... (unintelligible) ...suppose I'd say it depends.

Monk: Precisely. Bhikkhu limit their possessions to a robe, umbrella, and a bowl for alms. Everything else is a distraction that hinders his or her release from the world's suffering. Let's say, for example, that a synthetic hand is just that – a hand, a part of your body. But if it has  a watch installed in it? A blade?

Interviewer: Right, I think I understand. Where the line's drawn isn't completely clear.

Monk: Possessions – especially such intimate ones – are distractions that muddy the mind, that pull it further from inner peace. I believe the phenomenon of cyberpsychosis is proof enough of this truth.

Last night on TV, I saw the following scene – a Militech squad in some debris-ridden corner of the Middle East, fighting the "enemy" – terrorists, political opponents... Shit, maybe they were just actors? It doesn't matter – it never really mattered in the first place. One of them was wearing recording equipment, scrolling a braindance. I can count on finding that fresh BD in any shop within days. Turn it on and bam! You're in a warzone. You feel what they feel. You taste the blood in your mouth and the reassuring grip of the scroller's rifle. But that's not the worst of it. The worst is how the editor will be sure to try to show off the rifle, get a good shot of the manufacturer's name. Another split-second and you'll be ready to buy the same exact one – even order it with the same dents and scratches. Free home delivery.\nOnly twenty or thirty years ago we were asking ourselves – when will we cross the border at which empathy becomes irrelevant? Now, standing in the shelled-out ruins of a home with a rifle in our hands, it's hard to believe that border ever existed.

It was a night like every other. An oppressive black smog choked the city, pouring into the wicked hearts and lungs that breathed there. Acid rain drummed against thousands of window panes, the cityscape like a surreal tessellation of piano keys. Thirty years came and went; nothing changed. I stood at the window, smoking cigarette after cigarette, my thoughts distracted by the memory of a woman I hadn't seen since the war's end.

And then I heard a knock a the door. Just like her... Just like thirty years ago.

"Come in," the hoarse words strained from my throat as I mechanically lifted my hand to the wall panel. The metal door slid open noiselessly, revealing a slender figure draped snugly by an inky-black neomil dress. She stepped inside, her gold-plated hips glinting as they swayed. Her lips were a deep ebony, but her eyes... Her predatorial yellow eyes pierced mine and scanned me from head to toe. For a moment, it felt like they were prying my very soul from my body. Then I twisted my lips into an ugly smirk; I remembered my soul was already long gone. I left it in the war, along with the flowers I placed on my mother-in-law's grave.

"Someone's out to zero me," she broke the silence with attention-demanding bluntness. The smooth allure of her voice clouded my mind. I never noticed her third hand – a mistake that would spell my doom...

"Impossible," I started with the beginnings of a roguish grin. "Who'd ever wanna kill a woman with hips and lips like yours? And a corpo, no less."

“We don't fear death. What's to be afraid of? Santa Muerte is a good friend, our close companion. We know how to talk to her and we know when there's no more room to negotiate.” This is one of the first responses I heard while asking residents of Vista del Rey about Santa Muerte (Sacred Death). Her worship, officially condemned by the Roman Catholic Church but heavily influenced by its rites – is unusually popular among those of Mexican origin, and especially in Night City. Few realize that the cult finds its roots in ancient times. It's highly likely that Santa Muerte first arose as a fusion of the beliefs of the Aztecs, Mayans and other indigenous residents of South America with those of the Catholic Church, first brought to the continent centuries ago by the Spanish conquistadors.

Our Lady of Holy Death, also known as Lady of the Night (Señora de la Noche), is a fascinating deity. Her wide-ranging devotees include prisoners, gangsters and drug dealers, but also police officers, prostitutes and others who work under the cloak of night – in other words, anyone whose life is in constant danger. Even at the turn of the 21st century, persecuted members of the LGBT community would also pray to her.

Santa Muerte offers her protection to anyone who asks for it while leaving an appropriate offering on her altar: rum and tequila, fruit, cigarettes, candy or flowers. Interestingly enough, it is believe she does not distinguish between morally sound and morally questionable requests. Her worshippers pray for health and happiness, but also revenge or the death of their enemies. Everyone, no matter their request, must remember one thing – every prayer offered carries a price. If you don't pay, Santa Muerte will take someone close to you. And she would have every right to do so.

Santa Muerte is not just another cthonic goddess of the underworld. She is the saint of the rejected, the excommunicated, of those who feel somehow unfit to ask God directly to intervene. It should come as no surprise, then, that so many Night City residents consider her their patron.

Cyberware Usage and Its Side Effects

Many people believe we live in a time when "impossible" has become an obsolete term. Ripperdocs can replace nearly any part of the human body with artificial implants, from your big toe to portions of the nervous system. My years in Trauma Team, however, taught me that the "impossible" is still very much possible. Even now, as we enter the twilight of the twenty-first century, we as medical professionals have not been able to eliminate all of the side effects that come from incorporating cybernetic elements into our bodies. Of course, everyone is familiar with the mental disorder most commonly referred to as cyberpsychosis. But it doesn't end there. Although advances in medical science for the greater part of a century have reduced its incidence to a minimum, cyberware rejection can still occur in a small subset of the population. These unlucky few can experience a range of complications, but the following are the most prevalent:

1. Immune Response – The body rejects the implant, causing scar tissue to continue growing to the point that it causes pain and inflammation of surrounding tissue as well as possible interference with the tech's electrical circuits.

2. Psychological Effects – Neurological implants have the potential to cause unpredictable change in the brain. Possible side effects include depression, apathy, hallucinations and sudden increases in addictive behaviors, such as gambling.

3. Implant Overdependence – Long-term use of certain synthetic body part replacements can change the brain's chemistry to make it accustomed to a particular type of implant. There are reported cases of permanent blindness after patients attempted to replace their Kiroshi optical implants with different models.

In the face of these known risks, what should our outlook be as consumers and medical professionals? To deny ourselves cybernetic enhancements on the 0.5 percent chance we could lose our vision forever? Or gamble away our life savings at the casino? The clear answer is "No." Cyberware technology has elevated human biology to the point where these what-if arguments serve against our best interests. The best advice I can offer for minimizing your risk is to read the technomedical profiles for all cyberware you intend to purchase before you install it.

GUEST EDITORIAL

Braindance editors have long strived to strike a balance between real, lived experience and technological, experiential purity. The more heavily processed the material, the more abstracted the pathways, the clearer the braindance recording; these fundamental elements of design have guided editors since the first wave of brain-to-brain experience sharing technology took hold. In their pursuit of balance, however, editors have clearly shown a bias for purity over naturalism over the years, even going so far to use it as a point of pride in the quality of their production.

But in the industry's latest push for greater purity has the purpose of the technology already been forgotten? Will we not find ourselves processing and filtering a braindance recording to the point that the emotional experience no longer extends beyond what we receive from film, television and video games? After reliving some of the latest titles on my feeder unit, this once-academic question now feels all too inevitable with the industry's current trajectory.

For a moment, let's consider why some reports suggest more and more users are searching for unlicensed titles on the black market (so-called black braindances, extreme braindances, or XBDs). Are we so sure it's the illicit content they are after? Or maybe the real draw is the residual "grit" we editors try so hard to remove? Distracting thoughts, irrelevant memories, loose associative threads, emotions stretching beyond the desired spectrum... What if this "noise" is not so superfluous as we believe it to be? What if these peripheral experiences hold the potential to elevate a good braindance to an exquisite one? We do ourselves a disservice by not exploring these questions before our blind crusade for braindance purity leads this industry straight into the bin of obsolete, flash-in-the-pan technology.

– J.A.

Death is the card of becoming. It signifies an imminent and difficult transition – the conclusion of one phase of life and the beginning of another. Inevitably, something gets lost during the transformation, but something else will rise to take its place.

Judgment is the card of renewal. The angel blowing into the horn heralds resurrection and liberation. This card foretells an important change that will result in healing or fulfillment. It is also a symbol of self-worth.

Justice is the card of conflict resolution. It proclaims the need for order, to see through lies and deceit, and a return to the natural state of affairs. Justice implies a just sentence, but also due process.

Strength is the card of resilience. It is associated with determination, bravery and internal struggle. One must have dedication in order to overcome obstacles and reach one's goal. Strength is about physical prowess and spiritual fortitude – the power that must be unleashed to achieve the impossible.

Temperance is the card of balance. It may symbolize self-restraint or the gradual shift toward a more mature state of equilibrium. Temperance is associated with being in control of oneself as well as the desire to achieve inner peace.

The Chariot is always charging ahead despite being pulled by its steeds in opposite directions. The rider who steers it constantly reins in the light and dark sides of the soul with the help of Reason. To ride in The Chariot is to experience highs and lows – ups and downs.

The Emperor represents patriarchal control and is pleased with the authority and power he possesses to shape the future. The Emperor makes the rules and enforces them for the common good. But prestige has its dark sides – the Emperor is dominating and ruthless and will climb over a mountain of bodies to achieve his aim.

The Devil is addiction, craving and passion. He brings fame and fortune, but at the price of losing oneself to a world of material distractions. The Devil lures unsuspecting souls into traps, but always grants them a choice. One can try their luck and take him up on his offer, but one should always know when to call quits.

The Empress is a card of femininity and motherhood. She is authoritative, knows what she wants, and exhibits refinement and sensuousness. The Empress symbolizes creativity and growth, and instructs us not to dismiss our unconscious impulses, but to trust our intuition.

The Fool is everyone – including you and me. Each step he takes on his journey feels like stepping into a brave new world. Ultimately, the journey will change him. But as the card shows, he's a trustworthy lad whose tireless hope drives him toward his goal.

The Hanged Man is the card of sacrifice. It says that a price must be paid in order to achieve enlightenment. The Hanged Man's forsakenness opens the path for rebirth into a new life, though this path is wrought with pain suspended in time and ultimately ends in Death.

The Hermit is a card of self-imposed isolation. It represents an escape from the hustle and bustle of the city, a turning away from constant newness toward Ye Olde ways. For the hermit, solitude is the road to the sublime – a road that is taken not with great bounds and strides, but with small, concentrated steps.

The Hierophant symbolizes a respect for tradition. It represents one who tries to maintain the established order, even though their very character is shaped by it. The Hierophant places his faith in institutions – for the alternative is pure chaos. Only by placing his faith in order can he draw strength.

The High Priestess is a card of mystery. It shows how all our secrets hang by a delicate thread and the struggle between common sense and intuition. The High Priestess symbolizes the cold, calm waters as well as the mysteries hidden in their depths.

The Lovers is the card of dichotomies. It points to the contradictions that clash within each of us and of the challenge of striking a balance between extremes. The Lovers is also the card of dilemmas, like The Fool who stands at the crossroads, unable to make his choice.

The Magician is the card of self-confidence and adapting to situations through intellect and sheer will. The Magician is a schemer who always has one last trick up his sleeve, who despite everything manages to stay afloat and remain in control of his own destiny.
The Star is the card of hope. In the darkest of nights there is a light that shines the path to home. The Star is inspiration, motivation and gives us strength to move forward.

The Tower is an omen of radical change, chaos and destruction. The lightning striking The Tower signifies a return to the old order that lies buried under the ruins, and a new order that will rise from it. It is a symbol of tragedy, apocalypse and self-destruction.

The Wheel of Fortune means that change is coming. One's destiny could turn out for the better or the worse, yet it is also bears the promise of new possibilities. The Wheel reminds us that nobody remains at the top forever, but also that not every situation is hopeless.

The World lies at the end of The Fool's long and winding journey. Wiser and more world-weary than he started out, the Fool faces a moment of reckoning. Some of us accept where our journey has led us to, while others embark on a new challenge. One thing in this World is certain – you can't have it all.

The Sun symbolizes success. It is a card of freedom, renewal and a bright future that lies ahead. The Sun also represents truth, for its light will always pull back the curtain of shadow that hides the world's secrets. It is also represents greatness and splendor.

His vision has survived in the majestic shapes of buildings, the complex layout of streets and the ever-industrious inhabitants themselves.

Feast your optics on Richard Night's urban masterpiece – standing tall after eighty years! Just remember to stay in the neighborhoods under NCPD jurisdiction. Night City wears many different masks.

Night City was founded in May 1994, but its story starts much earlier – the day the young visionary Richard Night founded Night International (today known as Night Corp). When the world descended into chaos near the end of the 20th century, Richard Night dreamed of a modern city free from oppression, poverty and the errors of the past – a city that would be guided by the invisible hands of corporate experts. Not long after, Night went into business with three huge investors – Arasaka, EBM and Petrochem – who financed the construction of a metropolis. Night City's original name was Coronado City – taken from the bay that it was founded on.

The following years witnessed global war and ecological destruction. The United States of America collapsed. Night's vision, which had been slowly growing on elites, suddenly felt necessary. They understood that humanity needed a bastion of law and order upheld by corporations. Coronado City started to attract even more investors. Unfortunately, not everyone agreed with Night's ideas. Shortly after, our father-founder was murdered by unknown assailants – still unknown to this day. In his honor, the city council decided to change the metropolis' name. Since then it has appeared on maps as Night City.

The next decade was marked by a period of anarchy. After Night's death, the city became a bed of lawlessness. The situation became so dire that in 2011 corporations restructured the council, allowing Night City to continue function in the form we know today. Even in spite of terrorist attacks, the 4th Corporate War, or the hostile ambitions of the NUSA, the city still lives and breathes, nurtured under the wings of Arasaka and other megacorporations.

Officers subject to the Office of the Mayor of Night City are duty-bound to protect Night Citizens and tourists throughout the city. In recent years the NCPD (Night City Police Department) has been the subject of various rumors. Out of concern for your trust and safety, we have decided to cut through the chaos of misinformation and dispel some of the most widely-circulated claims about us.

Three questions about the NCPD

1. Q: Will NCPD officers protect me in all areas of Night City?
A: Sadly, no. The NCPD can only ensure the safety of Night Citizens in districts such as City Center or North Oak. Areas such as Pacifica and Dogtown do not fall under our jurisdiction. It's also worth remembering that the NCPD does not patrol corporate territories, or any territory outside of Night City limits.

3. Q: Do officers in the MaxTac unit take civilians and their lives into account?\nA: Yes. The idea that MaxTac officers aim to neutralize cyberpsychos at all costs is a blatant falsehood. Their priority is to minimize damage and loss of human life. Unfortunately, accidents sometimes occur, and for that we deeply apologize.

Relying on their financial resources would be akin to corruption, which is something we would obviously want to avoid. Our officers are not as well equipped as their corporate counterparts, but they more than make up for it with their moral compass and sense of public duty.

DESI ABDI: should be able to quickhack drones, no prob
Archived Conversation: Desi Abdi and Lucas Malkowsky

In terms of the injustices facing us today, the runner-up to social immobility is corruption. We've put up with city council and NCPD palm-greasing for far too long. Something has to be done. Something CAN be done. That's why I'm refusing support – financial or otherwise – from any large corporations. Only a mayor that's fully independent can bring about real change in this city, and together we can make that happen.

I've always been an activist for social change. That's why I'm running for mayor of Night City, because I know what the people of this city need. I know because I'm one of them. Under the neat haircut and clean suit, I'm just a kid who grew up on the streets of Heywood. If anyone knows how hard it is to break out of the vicious cycle of poverty, it's me.

Thanks to the Night Foundation Scholarship, I had the privilege of studying at the Asukaga university in Berkeley. Out of thirty candidates, only five received full funding. I'm not saying this to brag, but because to this very day I think about all those who weren't so fortunate, about the millions who didn't get the same chance I did. Deep inside, I know I owe something to them – them and their children, who face the same barriers their parents did a generation ago.

Spread the word to your friends. Put my message out there, discuss, educate. Even if you bring one person around to our cause, secure a single vote, it'll be a huge achievement. Together we can change this city!

Get involved! From putting up flyers to simply coming to rallies and campaign meetings, there are plenty of ways to show your support! Your positive energy and engagement is what will make this movement a SUCCESS!

How can you show your support?\nFirstly, you can donate money directly to our campaign finance account. Every month we publish reliable reports for every €$1 that we spend.\nDon't worry if you can only make a small contribution. If every Night Citizen donated €$1 a month, we would have €$12 million in 3 months!
Heey. So I cant stop thinkin about our little adventure. FUCKIN AWESOME. Thats how you live life. ON THE EDGE :>
Who doesnt like explosions and races right? :) Lemme know if the rest of your plan worked out
Egh, day just like any other. Hope it helped you tho
Sure, we'll keep in touch. Thanks again – you're alright, V.
entries.maleVariant: Sure, I'll text or call ;) If I can't convince you to blow up anythin else, then at least we can go for a drink. Take care!

entries.femaleVariant: Pff, sound more nonchalant than a karaoke star from kabuki ;) I'll be in touch
When in mid-air, you automatically grab onto or vault over nearby ledges.

Quickly draw a weapon with <Input actionName="HolsterUnholster" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, or draw your most recently used weapon with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>. Cycle your weapons with <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

Arm and cook a grenade by holding <Input actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> then release the button to throw it.\nPress <Input actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to quickly throw a grenade.\nHold <Input actionName="GadgetWheel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the Combat Gadgets menu and select an item you want to use.
Use the item assigned to the Consumable quickslot with <Input actionName="UseConsumable" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>
Crafting allows you to assemble items based on Crafting Specs you can buy and find around Night City.
While crouched, you can move silently.

Cybernetic implants are mechanical replacements for the organic parts of your body. They can give you superhuman-like abilities which can improve your combat capability and help you survive in hazardous conditions.\n\nAlthough a common practice in 2077, the installation of cyberware is still an invasive, and sometimes dangerous, medical procedure. Only specialists known as ripperdocs are trusted to install cyberware safely.

In the dialogue system of Cyberpunk 2077, you can look around freely, decide whom to interact with, and interact with various objects. If you want to make a conversation more interesting, pay special attention to your surroundings.

Use <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> / <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to scroll through available dialogue options and automatically change your view.

Confirm your dialogue choice with <Input actionName="ChoiceApply" color="MainColors.Blue"></>

Quickhacks can help you distract enemies.\n\nIf you create a distraction, such as a sound, nearby enemies will be forced to investigate the source of it. This will give you a good opportunity to incapacitate them or sneak by them.
You can use the help of a companion to execute a double takedown – the perfect strategy for quietly disposing of two enemies simultaneously. Grab one of the indicated enemies.
Traveling around Night City allows you to discover and unlock Dataterms, which will then become available Fast Travel locations for you to use later.
Sneaking up to an unaware enemy will give you the option to <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">grapple</> them with <Input actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Scanning devices with your optical cyberware will show you useful information about them, such as their strengths and vulnerabilities.

Devices that have security vulnerabilities will be uniquely highlighted.

Look at the device and press <Input actionName="InteractionWheelScan" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to scan.

When you approach a ladder, you will automatically grab onto it and begin climbing up or down. Climbing down a ladder requires pressing <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Fast Attack: <Input actionName="MeleeAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>\nStrong Attack: hold <Input actionName="MeleeAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>\nBlock: <Input actionName="MeleeBlock" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Timing a block just before getting hit will allow you to deflect your enemy's attack and automatically deal them a counterblow.
Your maximum movement speed can be changed depending on which Perks and cyberware you have at your disposal.
The optical cyberware you have installed is equipped with modules for analyzing networks and their weak points. These scans provide valuable information about your surroundings and possible threats.

Scanning people with your optical cyberware can provide you with a lot of useful information, such as how strong an enemy might be, who is in their crew, or what type of weapon they use.\n\nAs a skilled netrunner, you can see a list of quickhacks which you can use against your enemies.
You can lift and carry dead, unconscious or otherwise incapacitated enemies by pressing and holding <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice2_Hold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Objects highlighted in yellow while scanning contain valuable info to help you with the current job.

Shoot with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Aim with <Input actionName="RangedADS" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Reload with <Input actionName="Reload" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Switch to melee combat with <Input actionName="QuickMelee" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Shoot with <Input actionName="RangedAttack" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>
Aim with <Input actionName="RangedADS" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Reload with <Input actionName="Reload" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Holster your weapon by double-tapping <Input actionName="SwitchItem" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Though a common practice, cyberware installation is still a dangerous and invasive procedure which can only be performed by qualified specialists: ripperdocs. There are several ripperdocs operating throughout Night City who offer a variety of different cyberware upgrades.\n\nSelect your desired cybernetic upgrade from the list and enjoy your new abilities.
<Rich color="MainColors.Gold">Hold</> <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> <Rich color="MainColors.Gold">to use your scanner.</>
Shooting while moving is less accurate than when in stable position.
In some areas of Night City, drawing your weapon might be considered a threat. Be mindful of how others around you might react.
Reloading an empty ammo clip takes longer than reloading a weapon with a bullet in the chamber.
While Smart Link is equipped, Smart weapons fire homing rounds that will bend your bullets' trajectory mid-flight.
Tech weapons were built for precision and their ability to pierce through solid cover.

Gigs are tasks offered by fixers in each of Night City's districts. When you enter a district, you will receive a text message from the local fixer that details all of the available Gigs, automatically marking their locations on your map. When you approach a Gig location closely enough, you will receive another text message with a task brief and your Journal will update with the information.
You can climb faster with <Input actionName="ToggleSprint" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Your Stash is a secure system for storing equipment and can be accessed from all of your available safehouses and vehicles. For example, if you store something in your car trunk, you'll be able to access it from your apartment later on.
While in water, you can swim upward with <Input actionName="Jump" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> or dive down with <Input actionName="ToggleCrouch" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Without access to air, you will begin to suffocate and receive damage, which can eventually result in death.
You can choose how to deal with enemies. Sometimes it's enough to perform a non-lethal takedown.
Go over heist with Evelyn Parker.
To access your phone menu, hold <Input actionName="PhoneInteract" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.
While running, you can leap over surfaces that can also be used as cover.

Accelerate with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Steer with <Input context="MovementActions" actionName="MoveX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Exit the vehicle with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Exit" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

As a passenger, you can lean out the window to use ranged weapons. Return to your seat with <Input actionName="Exit" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> or holster your weapon.

As a driver, you can only use a Pistol or Revolver.
To interact with various objects throughout the world, use <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Do not think I haven't noticed your efforts, V. I think the best way to value hard work is to give more work. Who knows, maybe soon you will even receive the most coveted contracts...

V, my dear. The hard work you have invested with me has multiplied your returns. People utter your name with respect. This is an honor, but also a responsibility. Remember that well - I have new contracts from highly-placed clients that do not tolerate forgetfulness.

Well done, my dear, I see that you treat your work seriously. Not only have you earned my respect, but those of more serious clients. I leave the best contracts in your capable hands. Treat them with respect.
I am not happy. That does not bode well... for you.
I do not accept failure. You would be wise to remember that.
I never took you for a coward, V. Go back and finish what you started. I trust you would not wish to disappoint me...?

My dear, you are becoming more popular by the minute. Your actions have turned even ordinary people's heads. I suppose vendors may treat you differently from now on... do not be surprised to see discounts.
Becoming more well-known, aren't we, V? This is good. More discounts, more products - such is the price of being popular in Night City...

I am starting to grow tired of being asked about you, V. It seems you have become an unlikely star of the district. Vendors will surely offer more products and at lower prices. As they say, do not spend it all in one place.

Excellent, that was the last contract in Westbrook. For the moment I do not foresee any new assignments for you. Treat this window of free time as an opportunity to think about your future. Correct me if I am wrong, but perhaps you do not want to run around the city toting a gun for your entire life. Bear in mind that you are not getting any younger. Time to grow up, hm?
Downright pleasure doing biz with you, V. Your work shows - eddies oughta show for it too. More gigs coming your way!
One thing's for sure, V, you're on your way to the top. I'm just glad I can help you along the way. New gigs are waiting ;)
Know what you are, V? The best merc eddies can buy in Night City. Keep it up and you'll have this city wrapped around your little finger. New gigs heading straight for ya ;)
You botched it, V! And here I thought you wanted to make a name for yourself in this city...
Welp, that's one way to fuck a gig up. Not what I had in mind AT ALL.
Look at you, girl! You're the talk of the town! At least, in our line of work. You'll see - folks don't mind knocking down prices a little to do biz with minor celebrities like you ;)

Dunno about you, but I'm starting to hear your name everywhere again. Oh, don't worry - that's a good thing! I'm guessing folks'll give you the special treatment - special discounts, exclusive items... you get the gist.
You even remotely aware that all of NC's gossiping about you? Sheesh, gettin' flashbacks to high school here... Anyway, big names open a lot of doors, not to mention wallets ;)
Welp, Watson's clean, like literally ZERO new contracts. You mopped up the whole district, so I don't got anything new for you. Chin up, V – I'll be in touch.
Well, that's a wrap for Arroyo! District's gotta recover from all the preem work you've done ;) I'll holler if anything comes up
You smell that, V? The sweet, sweet smell of cold, hard eddies? ;) You do good work - you get more work. Beautiful system we got goin, ain't it?

V, you crazy bitch! You're blazing through these gigs like a wildfire! Just wish everyone was like you. You know, the name "V" doesn't just look like some pretentious nickname anymore - it's starting to carry some serious weight. Nothing to lighten the load like a few more gigs! Don't worry, I saved the preemest ones just for you :*
entries.maleVariant: V, you crazy bastard! You're blazing through these gigs like a wildfire! Just wish everyone was like you. You know, the name "V" doesn't just look like some pretentious nickname anymore - it's starting to carry some serious weight. Nothing to lighten the load like a few more gigs! Don't worry, I saved the preemest ones just for you :*

entries.femaleVariant: Woop woop! Welcome fucking big leagues, baby! You either go big or go home, am I right? Told ya we'd go places. All right, enough blowing each other off - time to get back to work. New gigs are waiting for ya, champ!

Well fuck me – I'm all out of work for you. Shit's crazy, right? At least nothing out in Rancho. All I got's some shitty gigs, but taking any one of them would be beneath your dignity, trust me. Ciao for now

Yo yo, V! You wanna put yourself outta biz or something? All the gigs in Santo've dried up – I got nada to offer you right now. Shit, I don't think this has ever happened before. You're really something, V, ya know that? Alright, take care!
You fucked up - it happens. Just make sure it doesn't happen too often, OK? Thx
Damn, that was weak. I need your A-game, not your D-game, all right? Maybe head down to the ripper's or something, get your ass into shape.
My driver is already waiting for you.
Sent you one of mine. He's rolling.

Been hearing a lot about you, V. People know they're dealing with a serious merc, not some Afterlife wannabe. You'll be seeing some fresh items under the counter, better prices too. See? Now everyone wants to do biz with V! ;)
Boy is your name making the rounds. Just so happens respect on the street is a valuable thing. In the long run, what matters is who you know and who's worth doin' biz with.

Shit, I remember when you first started doing mercwork... wet behind the ears as all get out. And now? Everyone's askin' about you, wanting to know what you're doing, who you're runnin' gigs for. Get this - people are even willing to sell you their stuff at half price just to say you bought from them. Congrats, V - I mean it.
Well, well, congrats! You flat out bought all the rides I had in stock. ALL OF THEM. When the fuck did you get so flush?! No, don't answer that. Less I know, the better.

Hello, V. I have an Arch Nazaré's that is looking for a new owner – practically new. It onced belonged to a corpo who wanted to impress his minions... except he did not have the first clue about handling it. He braked a little too hard and launched himself into the air – skull smacked the pavement so forcefully that not even TT Platinum could save him. Thank God for idiots. So, are you ready to buy?

Yo yo, got a new ride for sale – an Archer Hella. It's a fine car, but fair warning – it might reek a little of dead bodies. Bought it off the NCPD, who let it sit in a parking lot as evidence of a double murder. I mean, it's not like it hasn't been cleaned and polished, but if you end up buying it, I'd crack the windows for a while.

Hi, V! Got a Quartz waiting to be checked out. Fine machine, well taken care of, polished to a shine. Bought it off a certain gentleman who was a little whacked when it came to his car, huffing and puffing in his garage day in, day out. Until, that is, his wife filed for divorce – the ride had to go to pay the legal fees. Lemme know if you're interested.

I hope this message finds you well and in good graces. I am selling a motorcycle, and not just any kind – a Brennan Apollo. If you wish to be swifter than the thunderous smiting hand of our fickle Lord, go to the indicated coordinates and open your heart and wallet. I should mention that this is a one-time offer – it would be a sin to miss it.

"As they were walking along and talking together, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared." I have a theory that cars would please the Lord if He returned to our world – in particular, the tuned up Chevillon Thrax 388 Jefferson I have for sale. A car so mighty and majestic it almost makes you want to bow down to it. A great car destined for a great person. The question is, my dear V, are you worthy of it? Do some soul searching, check your balance and get back to me.

Beep beep! Got a Chevillon Emperor for sale. Won't deny it – hunk of metal's on the cheap side, bottom-shelf, but goddamn, the suspension on this thing's baby-smooth. Feels like you're riding on a cloud. And the seats! Fuck me, it's like you're getting a massage! Paint job's also so pretentious it's almost endearing. For what you're getting, this one's a bargain, trust me.

So this is kinda last minute, but I got a Herrera Outlaw for sale. Wouldn't wait too long on this – knowing folks around here, thing's a fucking thief-magnet. Probably only 1000 of them left in the world, no more than ten in all of NC, so we're talkin' 'bout a precious commodity. So chop chop, don't dawdle or I guarantee you'll be crying yourself to sleep for weeks to come.

Hey hey, got a Mahir Supron I need to get rid of. Now, I know I shouldn't talk smack about my own stuff, but... jesus, what a pile of shit. It's like someone welded an old tub and dumpster together, then stuck it in a cardboard cutout and taped some wheels on it. Look, I know not everyone's got enough €$ to blow on an Aerondight, but if you need something cheap, and fast – this is it.
Hello, V. I have a Makigai MaiMai for sale. Aside from sounding like a fruity cocktail, it is a little small – but you, your guns and your groceries will fit right in. What more do you need?

V, if you are planning on spending more time in the Badlands, I have just the car to suit your needs – an all-terrain Mizutani Shion. It might look like a fuel-guzzling beast, but it could drive over a field of nails and broken glass like freshly paved asphalt. It pains me to part with it, but such is the nomad's lot – we cannot get attached to anything.

Hey hey, there's a Mizutani Shion that's looking for a new home. Won't lie, might be a little beaten up. Previous chick who owned it liked to lead-foot the pedal, but the engine, suspension, brakes, everything that matters – all that's in preem condish. Rides like a pure dream. This baby's a classic, and a fast one at that – perfect for losing the 5-0. Oh, and the flooring might be a little stained. Coffee...? Blood? Hard to tell.

Hey, so the "Cthulhu" has just emerged from the abyss. Sounds scary, right? Seriously though – car's out of this fucking world. Barely even touch the gas and next thing you know you're burning rubber and your eyes are tearing up. Long story short, it's not for everyone. But something tells me if anyone can handle this beast, it's you. Buy it and don't look back.

I have a Quadra Turbo for sale, parked at the attached coordinates. I suspect it will not stay available for long, since it is a good machine and there is no shortage of buyers. If life has taught me anything, it is to seize an opportunity as soon as it appears, for it might only appear once. You can think about that while you gather the money to pay.

V! I come bearing good news. Scratch that, preem news! Got a Quadra Avenger for sale. Now this one's a fucking beauty, lemme tell ya. The paintjob, the interior, the rumble of that engine! Lookin' at her gets me a little hard, and I'm not even ashamed to admit it. A person who wouldn't buy this (and I mean stat) would be lame as hell. Just sayin'.

Greetings, sister. Would you happen to be looking for a new car? The kind that won't choke on dust every time you go through a turnpike? If the answer is yes, then check the coordinates I attached. I have the Quadra Type-66 "Javelina" that my brother-in-law tuned up. When I say he's a perfectionist, I mean he checks five times before tightening every screw and polishes every inch of frame until it sparkles. You won't find better quality for your money. The truth is, every nomad wants a car like this, but few can afford it. I hope you're tempted by the offer, because I would rather sell to someone I know rather than a stranger.
entries.maleVariant: Greetings, brother. Would you happen to be looking for a new car? The kind that won't choke on dust every time you go through a turnpike? If the answer is yes, then check the coordinates I attached. I have Quadra that my brother-in-law tuned up. The truth is, every nomad wants a car like this, but few can afford it. I hope you're tempted by the offer, because I would rather sell to someone I know rather than a stranger.

entries.femaleVariant: Yo, got a Quadra 66 up for sale. Previous owner was a SoCal and 6th Street-4eva type who liked to slam the gas racing the streets at night... till he slammed right into a corpo. Yeeaaah, can't say that ended well for him. But don't worry, the fender and windshield are brand new and the ride's in preem shape - all it needs is a new owner ;)

V! I have a great deal for you – a Rayfield Aerondight "Guinevere"! It belonged to the ambassador of Argentina... that is, until the country returned to martial law and the only thing waiting for him there was a noose, so he sold everything he could and fled the city. He didn't try to bargain with me – the sign of a smart man. I too would be smart if I were you and get your cash ready, because this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. The world ain't exactly teeming with these beauties. Everyone wants to be unique, stand out, be noticed – I know you do too. The Aerondight can make that happen.

Yo yo, V. Got some eddies to burn? Maybe, I dunno, you'd consider buying a Caliburn? You heard right – A FUCKING CALIBURN! Beautiful machine, a downright work of art. If I could, I'd make love to this thing. Used to belong to Cytech's CEO, but the gonk sold it cuz apparently, and I quote, "Only poor people drive two-year old cars." Shit, I wish everyone could be poor by that definition. I just hope this Caliburn gets a loving owner, cuz she deserves it. If you're interested, lemme know.

Hello, V. I have a "Little Mule" for sale – in other words a custom-tuned Thorton Colby. A techie friend of mine found it in a ditch outside of town – thought it was beyond repair. Nothing but rust, dust and a communal bathroom for rats, by the looks of it. But once he gave it a wash-down, banged it back into shape, swapped out the suspension and cranked up the engine... well, for riding around in the desert, you can't go wrong.

Hey! Letting you know I got a reeeally nice Thorton Colby for sale. Belonged to some car-jacker from Memphis, a certain Nicholas, may he rest in peace. He'd klep the most expensive wheels for rich buyers – you know, Rayfields, Herreras – but for years he always drove this Colby. I'd tell you why, but you'll know for yourself the second you get behind the wheel.

V, I have a "Gecko" for sale – the nomad take on a Galena. Solid machine, but I have to warn you, it's a little bare on the inside. By that I mean no cup holder, LED screen, tush-warmer or other gimmicks. That being said, on rough terrain this thing is smoother than looks give it credit – you'll be sailing over every dune and rocky slope. So if you're strapping yourself in for a longer haul, it will practically pay for itself.

V, my favorite merc! I got a Galena I'm selling. Hasn't been driven much – guy who owned for the last ten years was paranoid as shit of going outside cuz he was afraid "they" would zero him – car sat unloved for all that time. But you can't escape fate, right? Stray lead caught him through his window. Moral of the story's that you gotta grab life by the fucking balls. So don't be no scrooge, whip out your credchip and buy this baby.

Hey, got a Mackinaw waiting to be sold – you'll find it at the attached coords. Watch out for turns, cuz this thing drives like a fucking boat. It's almost like it WANTS to crash into streetlamps and pedestrians. Oh, and it's also a real gas-guzzler. Still, it's worth it for the kicks.

Hey, there's a used Columbus parked at the market, waiting on a buyer. Belonged to a choom who used to move drugs around town, so you might hang up an air freshener or someting. I don't mind the exotic smells so much, but each to their own, right? Lemme know what you think.

Yo, V! Got a Delamain for sale! Just to be clear – the car, not the corp. Bought it from a... well, not exactly sure who I bought it from, cuz the only "person" I talked to was the avatar of this bald, weird-ass English dude. But the car's great, good condish, mileage ain't too bad. If I were you, I'd take it. Head to the coords I sent and check it for yourself, then drop me a line.

Listen, V. I have a Cortes for sale. It once belonged to some trust-fund kid who got it for his birthday, except instead of driving it around he preferred to stay hooked up to porn BDs all day. Eventually the family disowned him, sold his car, and now here we are. So, you interested? Take a look and give me your answer soon.

Greetings, V. I have an Alvarado for sale in excellent condition, sitting in Rancho at the attached coordinates. I acquired it from a Valentino who had so many enemies he barely got out of town alive. Still, he managed to sell me everything he owned, including the car. You can tell it belonged to someone who was vain, glued to his earthly possessions... but I must say, the purr of the engine is like music to the ears. If you want it, just say the word – and make the transfer – and it will be yours.

V. In your line of work, one must be quick and punctual. Since you seem to struggle with both, I figured you could use a motorcycle. If you can have only one, let it be the best – the Yaiba Kusanagi. I happen to have one for sale. Buy it and you will not regret it.
Eds just came in. Always a pleasure doing biz, V.
Got the €$ – you made the right choice today, V.
€$ just came through. Enjoy it and drive safe!
Not bad at all. You'll hear from me yet again.
I'll be brief - you've completed every gig to be had in West Wind Estate. Happy hunting elsewhere.
Your accomplishments haven't gone unnoticed, V - you're starting to make waves in this business, which means more contracts on the table. Keep it up and there's more where that came from.

Guess who's the merc of the month? That's right, V - I'm raising a glass of Champaradise to you right now. Maybe I'll frame a still of you up on my wall... too creepy? Either way, I have a little reward for you - more gigs. Enjoy them.
Mercs like you aren't easy to come by, V... I've been saving my top-shelf gigs for someone I can trust. Now that person is you. Keep a lookout for them.
I happen to value a little something called professionalism. I also loathe those who don't adhere to it, as you just have. Have I made myself clear?
That's not how we do things, V. In this biz... well, I'll spare you the lecture. You fucked up. Badly.
The car is on its way.

In this city, the work you do speaks for you. Good work builds trust - and respect. That's not something my neighborhood ignores. Don't be surprised if you see vendors with discounts and new products.
Your reputation is starting to precede you, V. As it would turn out, by some mysterious stroke of magic, the prices at vendors have gone down for you - and only for you.

Well well, I guess this wraps up our marvelous little journey together. Everything's been handled – peace reigns over CC and my pockets are burstin with €$. Bout time you broadened your horizons, eh? Good luck out there! DD

I think about her sometimes, what happened to her, where she ended up. Maybe like me, hidden from the world, frozen in space and time. Her consciousness floats over the wires, mixing and melting, losing its shape.

Soulkiller. A copy of a person. Again – it's the same as it always is. It was supposed to be freedom, an escape from death, a backup. But tech knows no morality, tech is a tool, and the most powerful control the tools. Instead of freedom, it became the chains. Instead of dealing a major blow to the system, it became just another weapon in its arsenal.

Sometimes I think I can hear her voice, like an echo. But it''s so far, so different. And when I call out for her, nothing. When I try to track it down, I don't understand the traces left behind, where they lead, it all feels so alien. It's beyond what I can perceive, beyond what my mind can process. But maybe that's good, maybe it's best we never meet.

It often happens that our memories are superseded by people's stories. But who we are is built on the past, and the past is built on lies.\n\nIn 2023 Johnny Silverhand carried out an attack on Arasaka Tower. Fifty years later, those events became the memories of a certain V.

So you've decided to find the chick who put on this first-class shitshow. She had a job and you took it 'cause there was no one else to knock some sense into your gonk head. I'm here now, but so what? This search and rescue bullshit's a dead end, but that's not about to stop you. Maybe Evelyn will, who knows? Sure seems like she doesn't wanna be found.

The kind where you can barely breathe because you know what comes next?\n\nYou ever get those? I know you do. So here – welcome to mine.

Well, we know the Voodoo Boys were behind all this, so that's one step forward. Problem is, now we have to reach them somehow – two steps back. There are a lot of things to be found in Pacifica, just usually not what you're looking for. Good news is you already got your fixer: a man without a face to help you find this fart in the wind. Sounds like a fun fuckin' delight.

If someone told me I'd be taking calls from Saburo Arasaka's fucking bodyguard, I'd've laughed in their face. And now we're supposed to meet with some Takemura? Hand over all our detes? I'm not even gonna pretend like this is a good idea. But fuck it – sometimes you just gotta go all in.

Know what my downside is? No matter how much I might want to, I don't fucking make mistakes. Lo and behold! Our factory-reset ronin, hounded by every single Arasaka soldier in Night City for KIDNAPPING Saburo Arasaka's daughter. Kudos to him – I couldn't've fucked this plan up better myself. And after all this, he STILL wants you to drop by? I don't know who's more whacked – him or us. Just remember to knock four times. His head, preferably – against a fucking table.

That's all, folks! Little Johnny can go to sleep while the grown-ups fix their big ol' mess. All I know's that you cut a deal with Arasaka – you help Hanako knock Yorinobu off his pedestal in return for help with the Relic. You already know where I stand. You've got better things to dream about then a rockerboy's mad ravings. Just make sure this little dream of yours doesn't turn into a nightmare.

Go to hell, V. You're on your own, got that? Stage is all yours. I'll just stand in the wings and watch you meet certain death, 'cause that's how this little coup against Yorinobu is gonna end. That is, unless our porcelain doll's got any aces up her sleeve. But if things go south, just jump out the window. Don't give them the satisfaction – don't let the fuckers take you alive.

Well, chica, looks like we got ourselves into a real fix. No chance in hell I'm wriggling myself out of this one, but you're still alive. And as Misty says, "As long as you're alive, there's hope." Fate's given you a second chance, so use it – get back on your feet. Do that, and consider your best friend's last wish fulfilled.

entries.femaleVariant: Finally doing things my way: we grab that 'Saka son-of-a-bitch by his corposuit collar, leave a bloody trail of destruction in our wake. Toss in a swipe at Kang Tao, too. Look at you, V. Just might make something of you yet. Anyway, one thing's for sure – we're close. Sure hope Hellman spills what he's got. And that what he's got is answers.

If I've learned one thing from joyhouses, it's to quit while the going's good. Stare at those fake smiles too long, and all you'll see is misery. As far as clubs go they're all pretty pathetic, but at least it's in their own way. You know the chances of finding Evelyn are close to zilch, right? Like that's gonna change your mind... Anyway, let's go pay a visit to this so-called Fingers. But if we don't find Parker, you owe me a drink.

Every city's got its shady neighborhoods and "no-go" zones. Stepping into these areas in Night City is like wading into the abyss and feeling it stare back through your soul. Anyone with an ounce of sense avoids these haunts altogether. Your average gonk's usually seen limping out, bleeding from one or more places. And you, V? Just make sure you come out intact.

There's nothing you can't take away from a person – you just gotta look hard enough. When all options are exhausted, you've still got a body that can be harvested, skills that can be put to good use... Oh, and let's not forget "dignity" – that's a classic. Hell, I'm starting to think I could've done worse than end up on this little Relic of yours.

It actually fucking worked. Working with the Voodoo Boys, Brigitte… It leads us straight to Alt. Looks like your troubles are over, kid. Fixing your head is gonna be a walk in the park for Alt, that I guarantee. You just do what Brigitte says for now – I'll handle the rest.

So we're really doing this – breaking into Arasaka Industrial Park to hack Hanako's float for the parade in honor of her corpo-vampire daddy. All this just so Takemura can get an audience with her! You know, I've done a lotta gonk shit in my day, but I never got in the same bed as the fucking ENEMY. I dunno what's waiting for us at the end of this road, but I'm waiving all responsibility. This is on YOU.

Since I obviously wasn't invited to Saburo Arasaka's funeral, I guess this sad little parade will have to do – I'm just missing confetti. But in all seriousness, Takemura must have a death wish. He's just gonna jump onto Hanako's platform? Be my fucking guest – we'll deal with the snipers. Meanwhile, keep an eye out for an escape route. This is gonna go all kinds of wrong – I can feel it.
Unpause the recording and watch the scene.

I'm sick of this Placide motherfucker as much as you, but at least the fog has lifted, the goal is clear. You find a netrunner in the GIM and the Voodoo goons will set up a meet-n-greet with their queen. Pros? Maybe I'll actually get to see a legit netrunner, 'cause it's sure starting to feel like an extinct species these days. Someone who's got the guts to square off against the Voodoos has given me some hope, at least. But the cons? Damn near any minute your brain could start dripping out your ears. Afraid we won't have time to make pilgrimmages to the monuments of Pacifica's Golden Age.

I was gonna say that this time you'd have to go it alone, but it looks like the Aldecaldos've got some fight in them after all. Wonder what you see in them: a partner? Friend? Family? Something tells me sooner or later you're gonna have to choose one of the above, especially if it's thanks to them you get into Mikoshi.

Last stop on the line. Little does the corp know that this train's not going back. It's a shame I won't be there with you, 'cuz it's looking to be one helluva ride. But hey, that's what family's for, right? Anyway, once you get to the Arasaka sublevels, that crater filled with chrome and concrete, just take a second to remember that Johnny was there. Then mow down anyone in your way and get to Mikoshi.

You're almost there, V. In the heart of fucking darkness. Can you feel it? You're so close to the moment of goddamn truth. And I'm right there with you. Still. Always. Even if I'm just a blacked-out passenger in the backseat. Whatever you do, do it for us. At the very least, that's what I'm fucking counting on.

V? Don't know if you can hear me. Not even sure you're aware what's going on. What I do know is you got serious guts to make the decision you did. And I promise I'm not gonna fuck this up. I'll convince Rogue to take Arasaka Tower for one more wild ride.

Worst is behind us now. Rogue was shaking worse than all those corpodicks put together, I could tell. But she still said yes in the end. We're going back to Arasaka Tower and this time… we finish things right. We'll cut Alt loose in the Tower's system and she'll punch our ticket to Mikoshi. Fuck, how I wish you could see it!

Silverhand: The Creator (and Destroyer) of Samurai

Hidden somewhere between the Arasaka propaganda and Silverhand's own self-curated image, there exists a real story behind the frontman of Samurai. The fact of the matter is no one truly cared to find it. Labels, legends, slogans to chant – that's all anyone ever wanted from him. But by digging meticulously into all the dirty details of his life, all of the inconsistencies and exaggeration come to light.\n\nOne of the biggest gaps in Silverhand's life was the period he spent with nomad communities. Hidden from civilization, Johnny could have acted like himself and removed the mask he wears in public. If the world could get testimonies from the people who had contact with Johnny during this period, not only would every biographer be grateful, but – more importantly – experts might have a real chance to offer a clinical diagnosis for one of the rock scene's most iconic personalities.
"Samurai" Thirty Years Later: Facts, Myths, and More Myths

When Silverhand formed Samurai, he did so as a fully-fledged artist. He knew what he wanted, and as the group’s charismatic leader, he knew how to impose his vision on the rest of the band.

The roles in the group were clearly divided. Johnny and Kerry Eurodyne were the inspired provocateurs, the continually conflicted soul of the band. Meanwhile, Henry (bass) lived in his own world, even in those rare instances when he wasn’t high out of his mind. He may never have known how good he was. Rumor had it Silverhand was sleeping with Henry to keep him in the band. Silverhand was also rumored to be sleeping with Kerry to boost the latter's morale. The truth is, Johnny was sleeping with everyone, though his heart wasn’t always in it.

Soon after Samurai’s breakup, Henry suffered a literal shock in an accident, after which he began behaving even more strangely than usual. And then, almost as if he’d been ready and waiting to jump at the chance, he hit rock bottom.

Nancy (keyboards) was the single reasonable, normal person in the group – she came to a gig, played to the best of her ability, then went home. Only thing was, her toxic, aggressive piece-of-shit husband was at home, too. He ended up tightening his grip on her enough that she left the band. Soon after, he tried to turn the screw some more, but something in Nancy snapped. She finally remembered her murky gang past, and her husband had more than enough to think about as he fell eighty floors down. After seven months spent in jail, Nancy returned to Samurai, but it wasn’t the same. In the end, she left again for good and started a new media career as Bes Isis for N54 News.

Denny, drummer and high-functioning neurotic plagued by thousands of real and imagined obsessions, was only truly herself on stage. Off stage, she spent most of her time trying to prove to herself she wasn’t as fucked up as everybody seemed to think. That’s likely why she took up with Henry – compared to him, Denny was normal indeed.

If it hadn’t been for Silverhand’s legendary hatred of managers, those slick ass-kissers who told you what to say and when, when and where you were going to play and who you had to play nice with, Samurai could have achieved much greater success. Instead, they always remained a punk alternative, icons of cool and uncompromising rebellion. One day, you can’t get into one of their gigs, the next you could walk right by a whacked-out Silverhand puking into the river. And that’s what Johnny would call true freedom, before barfing on your shoes.

Silverhand’s death was what truly launched Samurai into the realm of legend – and out of reality.
