entries.femaleVariant: Shame you didn't try to save him. Badge friend of mine sent me his spec – guy's head was a mess, must've been taking 4x doses to make it through the day. Corp cut off his health insurance, cash dried up, ticking time bomb exploded. Maybe if he'd just gone back on his meds, things could've ended happily ever after.
Got some good news – there's a happy ending to your favorite TV show after all. Our psycho-star's alive and well. Flicking you the detes.
Got some bad news – turns out there's no happy ending for your favorite TV show. Our psycho reality star's dead. Flicking you the detes.

Sucks pretty damn hard you couldn't save her. Maybe if she could've separated the real world from her TV life, we would've stood a better chance of helping her. Sadly for her, she didn't just die a TV death this time.

Glad she's alive. Maybe there's a chance she'll start telling apart real life from TV life so we can start helping her. I'm just worried what'll happen when she finally realizes that massacre wasn't fake blood and artificial limbs.
He's outfitted in full military gear, so he could be a vet suffering from PTSD... but why the getup? Maybe he felt the cyberpsychosis coming on and wanted to look the part? Something doesn't add up…
Gangers picked the wrong choom to fuck with.

Most of the bodies are Tyger Claws – they're the ones who kidnapped poor Sofia and turned her into a doll. Little did they know her daddy was ex special forces, who went on a Tyger Claw hunting spree all over NC like it was a goddamn safari until they'd give back his daughter. Eventually the gang set up a meeting for the swap, but surprise, surprise – it was a trap. Sofia was already dead in the trunk. That was the second (and last) time they underestimated him – made short work of them on the docks.
Wasn't easy, but I managed to keep him alive.
Couldn't get close to him - put up a hell of a fight. Left me no choice - had to zero him.

Tygers took a liking to the girl and decided to turn her into a doll. Big mistake. LIttle did they know her daddy was ex special forces - wasted no time in hunting their sorry hides down. Only option they had left was to lure him into a trap. Bigger mistake. Don't underestimate an ex commando who wants his daughter back - he hunted every last Tyger as easily as if he was on a goddamn safari.
Glad you made it out in one piece and left our guy alive. Too bad NC's apex predators already sniffed him out - meaning MaxTac. Probably best if we get out of their way this time.
Glad you made it out in one piece. Our guy put up a hell of a fight, so there was nothing left to do but defend yourself.

One of the workers went psycho, started smashing up the construction site. Seems some of the workers tried to stop him, but their little poly one-shots couldn't pierce that exoskeleton of his. Anyway, they either ran or got added to the construction, if you catch my drift. Go check it out for me.
Guess even pneumatic arms can't lift morale in a toxic workplace.
Managed to take the cyberpsycho alive, though he sure put up a fight. Sending you the detes.
Cyberpsycho sure had drive. Had to zero him. Sending you the detes.

My, my, now that's some creative management. Seems this developer has no problem creating a wide range of business needs and solutions. I'm sure his long-standing connections with weapons dealers, the NCPD and other shady souls help enormously. And if a certain need isn't great enough, well, there's always the usual solutions of arm-twisting and kneecapping. The key to success remains flexibility, especially of the moral sort.
Really glad you got him alive. Poor guy almost completely spiraled out before he even realized what was happening.
Shame you couldn't save him. Poor guy almost completely spiraled out before he even realized what was happening.

Something about this ritual went wrong... seriously wrong. Place is covered in guts and blood. Must've had something to do with uploading the brain into the net and straddling the border between life and death. Only the girl who jacked in couldn't handle it. She went psycho and starting tearing into her chooms. I thought women were more resistant to cyberpsychosis... Anyway, at least we have her alive.

Something about this ritual went wrong... seriously wrong. Place is covered in guts and blood. Must've had something to do with uploading the brain into the net and straddling the border between life and death. Only the girl who jacked in couldn't handle it. She went psycho and starting tearing into her chooms. I thought women were more resistant to cyberpsychosis... Anyway, unfortunately I had to put her down.

It's true women are less likely to get cyberpsychosis - all the better we have her alive for more research. I thought nothing could surprise me anymore... boy, was I wrong. Wonder what she heard through those cables, what caused her to crack... I'll keep looking into it. In the meantime, I'm sending you your cut - bonus, included. Property developer tossed in token of their gratitude for freeing up the building that Maelstrom was squatting in. Not bad, eh?

It's true women are less likely to get cyberpsychosis - too bad we couldn't bring her in alive for more research. I thought nothing could surprise me anymore... boy, was I wrong. Wonder what she heard through those cables, what caused her to crack... I'll keep looking into it. In the meantime, I'm sending you your cut - bonus, included. Property developer tossed in token of their gratitude for freeing up the building that Maelstrom was squatting in. Not bad, eh?
Adam Smasher is destined for the scrapyard. Claim your reward!

You were almost right - turns out it was a prisoner who went cyberpsycho and managed to escape. Coincidentally, just happened to be an Aldecaldo buddy of a prisoner I rescued from the same outfit. Had no choice - took him out the hard way.

Well, that was unexpected. I'll relay this info to Dakota - Aldecaldos will definitely wanna know what happened to one of their brothers. Saul was too valuable as a pawn, so it looks like they tried to beat as much useful intel out of this poor gonk and make Saul watch, hoping that he'd crack. Eventually they took him for one of their "rides" through the desert... and that's when things got out of hand. He probably mistook you for one of them. I'll spare Dakota the sad news it was you flatlined him. Makes no difference now anyway. Better for them to think he went down fighting.

Psycho was a young runner looking for her input who vanished somewhere. Had herself convinced he was kidnapped but never got answers to the "who"or "why." She was hoping one more day in the Net would dig up the trail she needed. Days turned to weeks and she drowned in the digital ether. I didn't manage to salvage what little was left of her. Had no choice but to end her suffering or she'd have ended mine.
There's no way this ever ended well. Even if they did reunite it wouldn't be with their old selves.

Our kid was a Valentino, not a Maelstromer. Borg fiends must've had an axe to grind with him, cause they stuffed him with implants like a fucking Christmas turkey and just watched and waited for him to blow. Same would've happened to anyone chipped that fast. Body didn't have time to adjust to the 'ware and turned him psycho. Couldn't bring him in quietly – had to put him outta his misery.

Looks like our guy didn't even have to piss them off. While ago Maelstrom put out word it was looking for volunteers to test some new 'ware – obviously nobody stepped up so the borg-fucks just started scooping peeps up off the street. Valentinos been looking for this kid for a while, not to mention the runner who swarmed the net with data-feelers trying to track him down. Eventually must've broken free and fought for his life, made the Maelstromers reaped what they sowed. Whole thing backfired on them spectacularly. Kid was still just a kid – maybe with time he could've adapted to his new condition... learned to deal with it. Sucks you had to zero him – it's a sad day for Night City.

It's too bad you had to kill her. Mower was chipped with experimental combat implants. Who knows, maybe she had a glitch in her system – something we could've found to help her. Oh well... Sending your fee, but next time I'd appreciate some effort on your part.

Hey, got some info on Mower. Turns out she used to be Militech spec ops. She was feeling seriously off and called the corp to send help. They sent a fire squad instead… Listen, she didn't make it but that's cuz self-defense was my only choice.
Cyberpsycho Sighting: Where the Bodies Hit the Floor
I see. Looks like he's not the only wild attack dog in this story…

It was a gang dispute. The guy was one of Brick's people – tried to take revenge on Royce. You can guess how his solo attempt at a vendetta panned out – got pumped full of drugs, tortured and made into this wild attack dog of a bouncer. Had to flatline him, but honestly I doubt there was much left to salvage of him on the mental end.

Already told you, I don't give a shit about no warnings or restrictions or special terms of use. Think we both know you're not about to give me a warranty on this shit, so don't make me pay out my ass for nothing. Save the scop and let's do biz. Don't matter if the they're salvaged from old military bases or fished outta some back alley ripper's dumpster. Shit, could dig them up outta an Indian burial ground for all I care, long as they work. Hydraulics should be able to handle 2 metric tons, nothing else matters. My people will buy whatever I sell them, so just get your people to give me what I ordered.

Let me be plain. You've been in this biz long enough to know it's a rough way to make a living. This job should toughen you up, but instead you keep coming to me looking for a shoulder to sob on. Now, most companies just swap out their workers when they get tired, but not me – here I tried to show you some compassion, I even rounded up some gear for all of you at a decent price, and what do I get in in return? Ungrateful lunks like you just think about yourselves, your own comfort, company be damned. But it's thanks to me you got decent implants and a low-rate loan to cover them. And I did it for you, out of the kindness of my heart, so you didn't have to waste your time going from bank to bank, filling out forms you can't even read.  But do I get so much as a "Thank you"? Never. And you know if it weren't for Mary and Charlie, I would've kicked you out on your ass a long time ago. So try thinking about them for once and get back to work instead of crying to me. This is construction, for crying out loud! This is no place for sissies and crybabies! But hey, if you think otherwise, you can go ahead and pack your shit up. And don't dare show your face here again. I mean, show it once a month, when you come back to pay your installments, plus extra to cover that employee discount you won't be enjoying no more.

I gotta say, that Mary of yours sure has a head on her shoulders. She got you here at the last possible moment. Your body's rejecting the implants, and no wonder – it's not ready for them. They're military-grade, you can't use them without the proper training. Christ, they're not for civilian use at all. I can give you a scrip for painkillers, but don't forget – the pain is your body's way of warning you. If you ignore it and keep using that chrome, you could cause permanent damage to your spine. You might be able to take off that exoskeleton now, but if you break your spine you'll never move on your own again.
Turns out Cedric met the same sad fate as the other Red Ocher members that Biotechnica was experimenting on. Scavs decided to kick him while he was down and that's when he snapped - as would anyone.
First the corpos, then the scavs and now you. Who knew you'd be at the end of that downward spiral.

Had to off the guy. Name was Zion Wylde. Had some burnt-out military-grade combat implants. Plucked his victims from the Raffen Shiv so that Loa gods would open up his passage to the sacred realm. Not sure if he prayed too hard or if those singed circuits messed with his head, but something went seriously wrong. Maybe you'll be able to find out more.

If that's how you're gonna operate, we're not gonna find out much :/ Might as well've sent MaxTac. Only thing I did manage to learn's that Zion Wylde was a war vet. What a way to thank him for his service...

Just so happens I found a little drug hustle going on at the port – a colorful assortment of to boot. Customers are mostly just poor locals. Got word a bunch of them are showing cyberpsychosis symptoms, and I'm thinking it's no coincidence that the latest drug-blend to make the rounds is a hit. Unfortunately you won't be taking any samples, because I already offed the supplier. All I can say is that the biggest buyers are usually heavily chipped and can't afford painkillers or implant-adapting meds, which means the ingredients are probably similar.

Thanks for the info. Shame our guy had to die. Corps don't like getting their hands dirty – AKA cutting deals with street scum. But hey, if a dealer mixing glitter with charcoal or some shit can increase their profit margins? By all fucking means! Even better if a few gonks get zeroed in the process – less dirt on the streets\nSorry for the rant – I've had it up to here with this shit. He was just another merc like you, except his luck ran out.
Norio is dead – the "air of murder" must've gotten to me.

"An Air of Murder" – or "sakki," as Fromm calls it in his book, "Zen Buddhism and Psychoanalysis." The old samurai masters were uncanny in their skill at sensing incoming danger. Clearly, this ability didn't pass down to the Tyger Claws – a price they paid dearly for. Some folks, like Norio, need to know the cause behind everything. He searched high and low for Julia's killers until he found them. At least he didn't die with lingering doubts.

The guy's dead. He must've had an interesting past to be that paranoid about security. Tried to make his own version of ICE but got one hell of a hot short circ instead.\nThe family ran outside to see what was going on, the security system tripped and well... Guy went crazy after. Sad stuff.

Poor gonk was so afraid someone would zero him that he turned his house into a death trap. Too bad his family happened to walk into it. Wasn't much hope left for the guy anyway, but it's a shame his family had to go like that.
Autoshop owner was on a rampage – had to take him down.

The way corps here gobble up small businesses... it's almost painful to watch. Before they even clock what's happening, the owners are locked out of their own premises and slapped with a colossal debt. Then they bust their asses for the corp from morning to midnight to make ends meet. Looks like this one preferred to take his own life than give up the one place that was his. See how quickly the American dream can turn into the American nightmare?
It was a VDB netrunner. Looks like he wanted to move up the ranks by taking over the GIM. Hired a merc, then tried to zero him, blowing his own cover from NetWatch. I flatlined him.
Guy was probably scared shitless in that Voodoo Boy den. Did you really have to kill him? I thought we had an understanding...

Hey, I got a cease and desist from Zetatech, they say I'm using that lift in my shop without a license. What is this?? I bought the whole shop from them, spent my life's savings on it. They want to get me again cause of some license? Could you check and see if they made a mistake somewhere? And what sort of eddies are we talking about here?

-----

From: Laurent Lawless
To: Gaston Philips
RE: License? What license?!

Gaston, I contacted Zetatech on your behalf and it does seem that the equipment in the shop was not included in the deed. You bought the shop building – four walls, the floor and ceiling, that's it. I asked about the price of the tech, but they're unable to give an estimate because the shop in which it's located has been bought out.

-----

From: Gaston Philips

To: Laurent Lawless
RE: License? What license?!

But I'm the one who bought it out! Think I would know.
So what do we do now?
From: Laurent Lawless

To: Gaston Philips
RE: License? What license?!
Now they have to buy it back from you, and since prices have fallen in the area, you stand to lose a fair amount. But then we have priority to buy it back, and if we want to speed up the process we could give them an offer right now to purchase the shop and equipment along with the loan approval for whatever is needed to cover the difference. That's the good news. Bad news is, the equipment costs about double the shop itself.

-----

From: Gaston Philips
To: Laurent Lawless
RE: License? What license?!

Fine, I dunno, go ahead and file that loan application so I don't lose my chance, then I'll think it over some more. Besides, what's a shop without equipment, I can't even work without it!

-----

From: Laurent Lawless

To: Gaston Philips
RE: License? What license?!

All right Gaston, it's all ready, I just need your signature and you can reopen.

-----

From: Gaston Philips
To: Laurent Lawless
RE: License? What license?!

Great, thanks for your help. It's hard to deal with this all by myself. I'm going back to work, finally!

Due to the failure to uphold the terms of Agreement No. UPL/12064 and failure to respond to Letter of Demand for Outstanding Payment No. 11055 in accordance with paragraph 628 of the aforementioned agreement, the real property shall become the property of Zetatech within two days of receipt of this document.\nThis decision is not subject to appeal.

Let this be a warning to anyone thinking about buying this shop. Don't be fooled by the fantastic location or top-shelf equipment. Because guess what?! None of it will be yours, even after you sign whatever agreement the corp gives you. What, you surprised? Well, so was I. I shouldn't have been, though. It was right there in front of my eyes, in black and white. I didn't want to waste my time reading some complicated agreement with more twists than that apple novel by a certain Virginia. I also didn't bother doing my research, or else I would have found out the shop changed hands three times already this year, and the previous owners disappeared without a trace – except their debts, that is. All I can say is, I've dealt with my fair share of gangs looking for protection money or a one-time heist, but nobody, and I mean nobody, has ever fucked me over quite like the suits at Zetatech. So I've got only one answer for them: a wrench to the face and a vise for their fingers.

Heard from a friend you deal with recon and risk assessment. My interest is the Grand Imperial Mall. Can I count on you?

-----

To: SpaceBoy_66
RE: Job offer

Your friend give you my rate too? For the GIM it's double.

-----

From: SpaceBoy_66
To: Eagle Eye Inc.
RE: Job offer

Fucking robbery but it's a deal.

-----

To: SpaceBoy_66
RE: Job offer

Meet at your place tomorrow early.

except he had defensive chrome and eeked out living and fucked me up bad

Ghosts? Ghosts don't exist, V. The dead can tell you that.
The underpass near GIM is like NC's Bermuda Triangle for the homeless. Sound like a piece of cake? In the heart of Pacifica, nothing ever is.\n\nEnter at your own risk.

So to recap – Abernathy is Jenkins' boss, Jenkins is your boss and he ordered you to off Abernathy. It's a classic damned if you do, damned if you don't situation. You kill her – you're fucked. You tell Abernathy – you're even more fucked. Why? Because for the past few years you've been batting for Jenkins' team. If you get the job done, and do it well, you might get a promotion, but forget sleeping at night, because who knows how soon you'll be in someone's crosshairs. Only proves the wide variety of opportunities Arasaka has to offer.

A good kid from Heywood with stolen corporate cargo in hand, border guards breathing down your neck and a brutal heat haze melting the horizon. This is what freedom looks like. And if smuggling's what it takes to live it, then smuggling it is. But if that's not motivation enough, there's a fat stack of eddies waiting at the end of it too. All that needs doin' is moving the package from A to B. Simple.

If there was an ad for Night City, it'd have Kirk's dumb, grinning face on it. He's slick, thinks he's smarter than he really is and is kind of an asshole, but whenever you call him, he's got the next Big Job that'll rake in millions – like stealing a car from a secure parking garage. 'Cause obviously the millionaires of the future are sitting in the Coyote Cojo scarfing down chili burgers... right?

Our crazed ronin shows no signs of slowing his roll. We barely get intel from Wakako about the parade and Takemura's already hatching some harebrained scheme in Japantown. He wants to meet at the market? Fine, let's parley, but you already know where I stand. Don't let him strong-arm you into anything. Who knows how many loose screws are bouncing around in that skull of his at this point...

Since I obviously wasn't invited to Saburo Arasaka's funeral, I guess this sad little parade will have to do – all that's missing is confetti. But in all seriousness, does Takemura have a deathwish? He's just gonna "jump" onto Hanako's float? Be my fucking guest – we'll deal with the snipers. Meanwhile, keep an eye out for an escape route. This is gonna go all kinds of wrong – I can feel it.

All right, looks like the fun's over. Your little joyrides come to an end. Now it's time to see what this baby can do. Which is blast some Raffens to smithereens. And by the way – feel a little sorry for Panam. Gotta feel like shit, seeing Saul proved right.

A Militech corpo-cunt lost an arms shipment, and if she doesn't find it, she'll be paddling up shit-creek with stumps for hands. I'm betting it's not even about the weapons – Militech could lose a tank and it'd make no difference to them. It's about principles. One thing's for damn sure – someone's taking the fall for this.

Turns out Meredith Stout will do anything to stay in the corp's good graces. Unfortunately that means her "colleague" might get demoted... or worse. All in all, Militech recovered their property, putting the Maelstrom freaks in a shittier mood than usual. A day like any other in Night City.

Every corp has a Gilchrist. First he steals from them, turns a fat profit on the goods, lies about it, narrowly avoids the chopping block, gets rid of all witnesses, makes someone else take the fall from him, and to top it all off – he gets a promotion. Can't help feeling sorry for the Maelstrom gonks in this scenario... but only a little.

This classic rifle manufactured at the dawn of the 21st century possesses a unique shape, design and color-scheme that delivers one clear message to enemy targets and competitive rivals alike: I am Death incarnate. With its sharp angles, raw steel build and a trigger that just begs to be pulled, one look of it is often enough to send streetpunks running scared from Arasaka's agents (as if they didn't already have good reason). Even today, more than a half-century after its conception, this rifle commands respect on the battlefield and on the city streets. Of course, flashier weapons with new features and higher rates of fire have been invented in that time, but, in skilled hands, the Nowaki remains a dominant force to be reckoned with.

Sometimes accuracy isn't all-important. Sometimes all you want to do is spray lead and witness the havoc wreaked once the smoke has cleared. In that case, seek no further than the Shigure. This submachine gun from the early 21st century might be getting on in years, and it might not have the firepower of more recent models, but – and this is no exaggeration – it can unload more bullets in one minute than all of Arasaka's unprosecuted counts of tax fraud. Meaning a lot.

One of the oldest weapons made by Arasaka from the early 2000s. These days it's a rare sight on the street, as it's a pistol that is – no point in sugarcoating it – outdated and difficult to maintain. Spare parts for it are no longer manufactured, and it's no longer compatible with most standard weapon mods. That being said, should it be held up to someone's head and have its trigger is pulled, the end result will still be as conclusive as with any modern firearm.

In recent years, the list of commonly feared numbers, such as 4, 13 and 66, has grown to now officially include the number 91. While the phobias of other numbers have origins well studied by science (e.g. tetraphobia derives from the fact that the Chinese words for "death" and "four" sound similar), we can still only hypothesize about the rise of 91.

Patients afflicted by a phobia of the number 91 often complain of recurring nightmares in which a giant countdown reaches 91 then suddenly stops. When they attempt to restart the countdown, it transforms into a bright yellow board with vermin crawling all over it.
This shared experience has already spawned unproven conspiracy theories which, among other things, claim that the dreams are transmitted via either electromagnetic waves, the digitized minds of a mysterious netrunner sect, rogue artificial intelligences, or classified nanochips installed by Night Corp agents. None of these outlandish ideas contain a grain of truth, of course, so what is it that causes the phobia to manifest such intense reactions? That much yet remains unknown but, as so many scientists often claim, "the truth is out there."

So, without full knowledge of the phobia's origin and its underlying factors, how can you treat it? Studies thus far have shown promising results for conditioning patients via induced dream-states in which the number 91 is inverted to the number 19. Although this method remains in clinical trials, experts optimistic the 91% success rate will only continue to improve.
A Novel Phobia: Fear of the Number 91

To interact with a nearby object, look at it and select which action you want to perform: <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice2" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice3" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice4" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Advanced cyberware will unlock the double jump, charged jump, the ability to hover in the air for a short duration, and a devastating landing attack.

Cycle through dialogue options with <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input actionName="ChoiceScrollDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>. Press <Input actionName="ChoiceApply" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to select one.

Some of them tie into your life path.

Some dialogue options will appear grayed out, meaning you do not meet the Attribute requirement necessary to make that choice.

Scanning Mode: hold <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

And the most important feature in Night City...
Horn: hold <Input context="VehicleAuxillary" actionName="VehicleHorn" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></>

Motorcyle Leaning: Use <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="LeanFB" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to lean. Up to lean forward, Down to lean back. Leaning only changes your center of mass. Lean back and apply the gas to perform a wheelie. Lean forward and apply the brake to perform an endo. Changing your center of mass affects how much traction you have at either end. Lean forward slightly mid-corner to induce oversteer, lean back slightly to induce understeer. In midair, lean forward/backward to do flips, and steer with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="TurnX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to spin!

Free Rev: hold <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Handbrake" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> and press <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> or <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Decelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>
Allows you to rev your engine while stationary, then launch at high RPM for a speed boost when you release the Handbrake. Or just rev your engine for fun!

Burn Out Mode: hold <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> and <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Decelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> simultaneously at lower speeds to engage.
While engaged, use <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="TurnX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to rotate the vehicle in tight spaces.
Also, if you heat up your tires a little, you can trigger a drag-race style, high-grip launch when you release <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Decelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> while stationary. The hotter the tires, the faster the launch!
Finally, on controllers with analog gas and brake inputs, try pressing them lightly to engage Burn Out Mode when coming into corners at low and medium speeds to induce a more controllable drift (works best with AWD and RWD vehicles).

Unstuck Rocking Mode: hold <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Accelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> or <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="Decelerate" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> when stuck.
Use <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="TurnX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to rotate your vehicle so its wheels touch the ground. If that doesn’t work, rock back and forth with <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="LeanFB" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.
If the vehicle is upside down, use <Input context="VehicleDrive" actionName="TurnX" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to flip it back on its wheels.

Call Active Vehicle: <Input actionName="CallVehicle" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>
Note: it will automatically park in the nearest available spot, provided you have street access.

All vehicles you’ve received or purchased are stored in your Garage. To mark a vehicle as active for the Call Vehicle function, access your Garage menu by holding <Input actionName="CallVehicle" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, browse available vehicles with <Input context="UIShared" actionName="navigate_up" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UIShared" actionName="navigate_down" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then press <Input context="UIShared" actionName="proceed" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to select one.

You can hijack occupied vehicles provided you meet the Body Attribute requirement necessary to pull the driver out of the driver's seat. You can steal unoccupied vehicles provided you meet the Technical Ability Attribute requirement.

As you explore Night City, you will come across and unlock Fast Travel Dataterms: <Image id="MappinIcons.FastTravelMappin" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>\n\nInteract with the nearest Dataterm to view a map with all currently unlocked locations. Select one with <Input context="UIShared" actionName="world_map_menu_fast_travel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to travel there.

Your Journal contains information about available, active and completed Jobs as well as their specific objectives. Open the Journal with <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenJournalMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> from the main menu.

You have a minimap in your HUD, but you can also open the full map with <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenMapMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> from the main menu. Use the map to track objectives from active Jobs and other useful leads. It also displays points of interests such as vendors, ripperdoc clinics, fast travel points and available work.

Hold <Input context="UI_DPad" actionName="PhoneInteract" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to access your phone, allowing you to call or message people from your list of contacts. If you want to open a message you just received, press <Input actionName="NotificationOpen" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> or navigate to the Messages tab in the main menu. These messages will often contain useful information about your current Job or Gig.

Night City is a living, breathing world that offers many places to explore. Pay attention to your surroundings and check your map and phone regularly.

GIGS: <Image id="MappinIcons.Gigs" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> These work opportunities are obtained from fixers throughout Night City. When you enter a district, you'll receive a message from the local fixer with a list of available Gigs and they will become marked on your map. When you near a Gig's location, you'll receive a message with additional details. These details will also be stored in your Journal.
NCPD SCANNER HUSTLES: <Image id="MappinIcons.NCPDScanner" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> These are jobs contracted out by the Night City Police Department. That's right – the NCPD is willing to pay mercs for settling public safety issues that they don't have the resources to handle themselves... Or maybe they just don't have the guts.

Cyberdecks unlock Netrunner abilities that allow the user to quickhack people and devices.

Each cyberdeck comes with a base set of pre-installed quickhacks, a limited number of slots for equipped quickhacks and a certain amount of RAM which is required to execute them. Different cyberdeck models can vary in terms of their stats and power. Higher Tier decks are able to perform more advanced quickhacks.

You can access your cyberdeck in the Inventory or Cyberware screens through the main menu <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenHubMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

RAM is a resource used when performing quickhacks. When you upload a quickhack to an enemy or device, it uses up a certain amount of RAM units. A quickhack's RAM cost can be altered in different ways, such as certain cyberware abilities, Perks and differences in level. RAM recovers automatically over time.\n\nYour maximum RAM can be increased with a higher Intelligence Attribute, certain cyberware abilities and Perks as well as by equipping a better cyberdeck.

Every cyberdeck comes with a pre-installed set of quickhacks. You can find specific details about them and about the cyberdeck in their descriptions.

To upload quickhacks, you must have enough RAM available on your cyberdeck. RAM cost can be altered by different means, such as your level, specific Perks or cyberware abilities.

To upload a quickhack, activate your scanner with <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, aim at the device, select a quickhack from the list using <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_MoveDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_MoveUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then press <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_ApplyAndClose" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to execute it.

Distract Enemies <Image id="UIIcon.Malfunction" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Causes a device to malfunction, resulting in erratic behavior that will distract nearby people.

Remote Deactivation <Image id="UIIcon.ToggleState" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Manipulates basic device functions, such as opening/closing doors and activating/deactivating cameras.

Camera Control <Image id="UIIcon.TakeControl" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Grants full remote control of the camera.

Initiate Overload <Image id="UIIcon.OverLoadDevice" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Overloads a device's electrical circuitry, permanently destroying it.

Friendly Mode <Image id="UIIcon.OverrideAttitude" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Overrides the target's recognition module, causing you to be perceived as an ally and authorization holder. Turrets and cameras treat your enemies as their enemies and assist in combat whether you are in combat or undetected.

Assist Mode <Image id="UIIcon.SetDeviceTagKillMode" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Forces a turret's targeting into manual mode.

Take Control <Image id="UIIcon.TakeControl" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></> - Enables remote operation of turrets and computers.

Cyberdecks have special slots reserved for antipersonnel quickhacks to use against your enemies, and can be customized to suit your playstyle.

Open your Inventory and click on the Cyberdeck slot to change which quickhacks you have actively installed.

To upload a quickhack into a target, you must have enough RAM available on your cyberdeck. RAM cost can be altered by different means, such as specific Perks and cyberware abilities.

To upload a quickhack, activate your scanner with <Input actionName="VisionHold" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, aim at your target, select a quickhack from the list using <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_MoveDown" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_MoveUp" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then press <Input context="UI_QuickHackPanel" actionName="UI_ApplyAndClose" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to execute it.

New quickhacks can be found throughout the world, purchased from vendors, earned as rewards, and sometimes acquired from uploading the Datamine daemon to network Access Points. You can also craft them if you possess the necessary Crafting Specs. Quickhack Crafting Specs can found throughout the world, purchased from vendors, and earned as rewards.

Every cyberdeck comes with Breach Protocol pre-installed, which gives it the ability to penetrate networks and upload powerful programs called daemons that can infiltrate all connected enemies and devices.

Every cyberdeck also comes pre-installed with the ICEpick daemon. Uploading it successfully via Breach Protocol will decrease the RAM cost of all quickhacks used on enemies and devices connected to the network.

New, powerful daemons can be unlocked in the Breach Protocol Skill tree.

Breach Protocol cannot be initiated without a cyberdeck equipped.

Access Points are physical ports through which it is possible to access the local network. They can be found by exploring your surroundings or by performing the Ping quickhack on a device or person connected to the same network.\n\nSuccessfully uploading a Datamine daemon into an Access Point can grant you money, quickhack crafting specs or components, and sometimes even an entirely new quickhack.

Ranged weapons are grouped by manufacturer and technology type.

Power weapons, when coupled with Ballistics Coprocessor cyberware, allow you to control your bullets' ricochet trajectory.

Tech weapons allow you to charge shots that can penetrate cover and walls to hit enemies.

Smart weapons, when coupled with Smart Link cyberware, allow you to lock onto targets and fire homing rounds.

Ammo is shared between all weapons that belong to the same category:
- Handgun Ammo (Pistols, Revolvers, SMGs)
- Heavy Ammo (Assault Rifles, Precision Rifles, LMGs)
- Shotgun Ammo (Shotguns)
- Sniper Ammo (Sniper Rifles)

Ranged weapons can be improved with attachments such as sights, scopes and muzzle brakes. Their stats can also be improved by installing mods. You can see available mod slots by selecting a weapon from your inventory. Melee weapons, which are categorized into Blades and Blunt Weapons, can similarly be modded.

Weapons can also be crafted and upgraded from the main menu:  <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenHubMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

Every piece of equipped gear increases Armor and other stats, while also representing an Edgerunner's style.

Armor decreases incoming damage. For example, approximately 10 Armor reduces incoming damage per second (DPS) by 1. Installing cyberware can increase your Armor as well as aid you in other aspects of combat.

You can swap out your gear in your Inventory, which is accessible from the main menu: <Input context="UIToggles" actionName="OpenHubMenu" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

A variety of mods can also improve your equipped gear's stats.

Although a common practice, installing cyberware is still an invasive medical procedure that can only be safely performed by specialists known as ripperdocs.

Cybernetic implants are designed to significantly enhance the user's physical and cognitive abilities.

There is a limited number of cyberware slots for installed cyberware on your body, so only one instance of a given cyberware type can be installed at a time.

Your equipped cyberdeck automatically activates when you scan a hackable target with your Kiroshi scanner.

Kerenzikov and Berserk are activated with <Input context="Abilities" actionName="IconicCyberware" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></>

Cyberware is activated with <Input context="Abilities" actionName="UseCyberware" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> if it has already been assigned to the Combat Gadget slot. To assign it there, hold <Input actionName="WeaponWheel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the quick-access menu, go to the Combat Gagdet quickslot with <Input actionName="UI_FakeCamera" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, cycle through available items with <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_DPad_Left" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_DPad_Right" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then select one to make active.

The Combat Gadget quickslot allows for quick use of grenades and certain combat cyberware.

Press <Input context="Abilities" actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to use.
Hold <Input context="Abilities" actionName="UseCombatGadget" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> for precise aiming.

To assign an item, hold <Input actionName="WeaponWheel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the quick-access menu, go to the Combat Gadget quickslot with <Input actionName="UI_TutorFakeCamera" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, cycle through available items with <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_PreviousAbility" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_NextAbility" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then select one to equip.

Combat gadgets can also be assigned in your inventory by selecting the Combat Gadget quickslot.

Grenades do not disappear from your inventory when you use them. Instead, they use charges, which recharge automatically over time. The number of charges, the recharge rate, and other grenade effects can be upgraded with certain Perks.

When you acquire a higher Tier of a grenade type you already possess, it will automatically replace the lower Tier version in your inventory. You cannot possess multiple Tiers for the same grenade at one time.

The Consumable quickslot allows you to quickly and conveniently use Health Items. Press <Input context="Abilities" actionName="UseConsumable" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> to use the item assigned to it.

To assign an item, hold <Input actionName="WeaponWheel" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to open the quick-access menu, go to the Consumable quickslot with <Input actionName="UI_TutorFakeCamera" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, cycle through available items with <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_PreviousAbility" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> and <Input context="UI_DPad_Wheel" actionName="UI_NextAbility" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>, then select one to equip.

Consumables can also be assigned in your Inventory by selecting the Consumable quickslot.

Food, drinks and boosters can only be consumed from the Inventory. To do so, hover over an item and hold <Input context="UIMenu" actionName="use_item" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>.

Health Items, such as inhalers and injectors, do not disappear from your inventory when you use them. Instead, they use charges which recharge automatically over time. The number of charges, recharge rate, and other effects can be upgraded with certain Perks and Cyberware.

When you acquire a higher Tier of a Health Item you already possess, it will automatically replace the lower Tier version in your inventory. You cannot possess multiple Tiers for the same Health Item at one time.

Food regenerates Health. Drinks regenerate Stamina.

Effects gained from consumables do not stack. A new effect will replace the current one.
Markers on the yellow track indicate a visual clue is available.
Look around for clues highlighted in yellow:
Markers on the blue track indicate thermal clues.

You can craft and upgrade items from the Crafting tab of the main menu.

To craft an item, you'll need the Crafting Spec for it as well as the necessary components.

Crafting Specs can be purchased at vendors or found in loot. A Crafting Spec's color indicates the Tier of the item you're crafting. You can craft weapons, weapon mods and attachments, quickhacks, consumable items, combat gadgets, ammo and even other crafting components.

You start the game with a set <Rich color="RarityColor.Common">Tier 1</> and <Rich color="RarityColor.Uncommon">Tier 2</> Crafting Specs for weapons and weapon attachments as well as all Crafting Specs for ammo and components.

Crafted weapons have fixed stats and a fixed number of mod slots.

Whenever you acquire an Iconic weapon, you can immediately upgrade it to next Tier, provided you have the necessary components. Upgrading a weapon increases its stats. Iconic weapons cannot be upgraded after reaching the highest Tier.
Markers on the green track indicate audio clues.

Weapons, quickhacks, daemons and some devices can inflict various long-term status effects on both you and your enemies. The duration of status effects on enemies is displayed by their name.

Bleeding <Image id="UIIcon.wounded_disabled_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- slowly depletes Health, disables sprinting and reduces jump height

Blinding <Image id="UIIcon.blinded_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- briefly reduces threat detection and hinders movement

Burn <Image id="UIIcon.burning_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- continuously depletes Health

Crippled <Image id="UIIcon.crippled_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- severely limits combat or movement effectiveness depending on which limb is crippled

EMP <Image id="UIIcon.EMP" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- briefly deactivates or severely limits the combat effectiveness of mechs, drones and robots, in addition to dealing damage

Knockdown <Image id="UIIcon.knockdown_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- briefly knocks to the ground, revealing Weakspots

Poison <Image id="UIIcon.poisoned" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- slowly depletes Health, reduces Armor and slows movement

Stun <Image id="UIIcon.stun_icon" align="bottom" width="75" height="75"></>- briefly immobilizes, leaving vulnerable to attack

You can read collected shards by pressing <Input actionName="NotificationOpen" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Hide"></> when the notification appears. They can also be found in the Shards section of your Journal.\n\nSome shards you find may contain data hidden behind encryption, preventing access from the authorities or nosy edgerunners. Select the CRACK SECURITY option to begin decryption through Breach Protocol and upload the Security Breach daemon in order to access the hidden content.

Health is a measure of your vitality. Your Max Health increases when you level up. It can be increased further by investing in your Body Attribute as well as in certain Perks and cyberware.

Outside of combat, your Health will fully regenerate automatically. It regenerates even faster when you consume food.

During combat, Health regeneration is not available by default. You can unlock this ability by acquiring the Painkiller Perk, which can be found in the Body Attribute's Perk tree. Taking a shower in V's apartment will also temporarily give you this ability.

Armor reduces the amount of damage you take from direct hits. As you progress, your enemies will gain access to more powerful weapons. Increasing your Armor will improve your chances of survival. Cyberware is the primary source of Armor, but some Perks and clothing items can help reduce the damage you take in other ways.

Stamina is a measure of your endurance. Certain movements that can give you an edge in combat, such dodging and sprinting, require Stamina to perform.

You can improve how quickly your Stamina is drained and how quickly it regenerates by investing in certain Perks and Cyberware.

Movement, shooting and melee attacks all use Stamina. Your Stamina will begin to regenerate automatically after a short time, but how quickly it begins and how long it lasts depends on the type of weapon you have equipped.

The lower your Stamina, the more your proficiency and accuracy with ranged weapons will suffer. Likewise, at low Stamina, your melee attacks will be slower and deal reduced damage.

Completing jobs and other activities will give experience points (XP) that increase your level.

Every level you gain, you earn an Attribute Point and Perk Point that can be spent to unlock a Perk within a Perk tree.

You can level up a Skill by performing actions related to that Skill. After all, practice makes perfect!

Attributes represent the possible range of your abilities as a mercenary. They can be improved by investing the Attribute Points you earn from leveling up.

Each Attribute also contains a Perk tree. Perks offer unique abilities and boosts to your gameplay experience. They can be unlocked by investing the Perk Points you earn from leveling up. These points can be refunded, so feel free to experiment!

By improving an Attribute, you receive a variety of bonuses:

BODY determines your raw physical power and fortitude. It improves your proficiency with Shotguns, Light Machine Guns and Blunt Weapons. It also enables you to open some doors by force, rip off turrets, and use intimidating or solo-trained dialogue choices. +2 Max Health per Attribute Point.

COOL determines your assassination skills and stealth abilities. It improves your proficiency with Precision Rifles, Sniper Rifles, Handguns and Throwable Weapons. It also enables you to use advanced, stealthy Perk abilities and subtle or street-smart dialogue choices. +1.25% Crit Damage per Attribute Point.

INTELLIGENCE determines your netrunning abilities. It improves your proficiency with Smart Weapons and allows you to unleash your full potential as a netrunner. It also enables you to access local subnets and show off your knowledge of the Net in dialogues. +1 Max RAM per 4 Attribute Points.

REFLEXES determine your maneuverability and ability to evade enemy attacks. It improves your proficiency with Assault Rifles, Submachine Guns and Blades, and enables you to use advanced movements. It also enables you to make quick, observant remarks in dialogues. +0.5% Crit Chance per Attribute Point.

TECHNICAL ABILITY determines your techie know-how. It improves your proficiency with explosives and Tech Weapons and allows you to be compatible with high-end cyberware. It also allows you to bypass some locks, override devices and exhibit tech-savvy knowledge in dialogues. +2 Armor per Attribute Point.
Skills represent your proficiency in various gameplay elements and can be improved by performing related actions. As you improve them, you'll unlock thematic bonuses.

Street Cred is the measure of your reputation in Night City. As your Street Cred grows, you will gain access to new vehicle offers and vendor discounts beyond the reach of small-time punks.\n\nNight City is bursting with opportunity, so get out there and make a name for yourself!

You can grapple enemies who haven't detected you by pressing <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>

You can still move while grappling an enemy, and can choose to perform a lethal <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> or non-lethal <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice2" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> Takedown.

The enemy will struggle to free themselves from your grip. If you hold them too long, they will eventually break free. High-level enemies, marked with a <Image id="UIIcon.q000_tutorial_icon_boss" align="bottom" width="70" height="70"></>, will break free more quickly.

Although some high-level enemies cannot be grappled, you can still perform Takedowns on them while undetected. Using certain abilities and items, as well as cleverly using the environment to your advantage, will help you remain out of sight. Some bosses might require multiple Takedowns to defeat.

Enemies and security systems may notice and react to bodies you leave out in the open. Make sure to dump the bodies in appropriate hiding locations (a dumpster, for example) or otherwise in areas that are not easily visible to enemies.

Hold <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice2" color="Tutorial.InputHint" hold="Show"></> to pick up a body, then press <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></> to dump it.

To dump a body in an appropriate container, approach it while holding the body and press <Input context="InteractionActions" actionName="Choice1" color="Tutorial.InputHint"></>. If you perform a Takedown on an enemy directly next to one of these containers, you will hide the body there automatically.

Remember: these containers have limited capacity, and once you've placed a body in one it cannot be removed.

All loot from dumped bodies is automatically dropped to the ground in front of the container.

An enemy is in a Combat State if it is actively attacking its target or approaching its last known location.\n\nWhen an enemy cannot locate its target, it will fall back to an Alerted State and begin patrolling the area to search for the threat, making it more difficult to sneak around them. If an enemy finds a body, they will remain in a permanent Alerted State.

Enemies patrolling an area follow a pattern that can be observed and used to your advantage.

Some devices allow you to distract enemies and divert them from their path. An enemy who is distracted will have a white outline.

Noises such as human footsteps or silenced gunshots can also alert an enemy, who will then try to locate the source. Louder noises such as a combat-initiating shout or a dying shout will make enemies enter an Alerted State or enter directly into combat.

Soviet cities may be bleak, dangerous and none too pleasant to look at… but they are clean. The Communist Party nomenklatura waged a domestic war on garbage. "Down with candy wrappers and broken bottles!" "We stand against cigarette butts in our streets!" Such were some of the rallying cries that were met with thunderous applause by party apparatchiks. These appeals, however, were not met with the same enthusiasm and dedication by miners, factory laborers and kolkhoz farmers. As a result, the responsibility for widespread waste collection fell to the USSR's experts in robotics, paving the way to the birth of the Kaukaz 271 Aras.\n\nThe Aras is an autonomous cleaning drone that quickly came to be known for its affordability and reliability (even if a bit clunky). To the surprise of the Soviet leadership and the General Secretary of the Communist Party, the Aras became a highly sought product for export internationally. It can now be found in major cities across the globe, including Night City. Many consider it definitive proof of the superiority of a centrally planned socialist economy.

In the past, approximately 4.5 million Americans worked as cab drivers, truckers or bus drivers. Today, that number has fallen to less than 300,000. Of course, one major factor to this was the catastrophic drop in North America's population due to wars, epidemics and climate disasters. Yet, even in the face of population drop-off, driving as an occupation for freight and passenger transport was nearly made extinct with the advent of self-driving vehicles.\n\nVehicles such as the autonomous Mahir MT28 Coach are now a common sight along major highways and interstates. For passengers, it has been a welcome change. Unlike human drivers, the Mahir MT28 Coach never needs to take bathroom breaks and is far less prone to causing traffic accidents. That said, autonomous vehicles bring their own set of risks. In 2068, on a non-stop route from Dallas to Tucson, a partial failure in the MT28 Coach's operating system caused the air-conditioning unit and door locks to malfunction. The bus reached its destination, but all the passengers had been cooked to death in their seats. Of course, the Board of Mahir doesn't believe the success and glowing reputation of the MT28 Coach's primary function should be marred because of the occasional minor error in its secondary systems.

"Basilisk" is a fitting name for this line of Militech armored vehicle. Much like the mythical monster that is its namesake, one look at this beast is enough to knock you on your back. As the characteristic silhouette of the Basilisk appears on the horizon, even the most formidable enemy forces will throw up their hands in unconditional surrender. An attempt at retreat is an exercise in futility – there is no escape from the Basilisk. This panzer, despite its tremendous size, moves across desert terrain with incredible grace and speed, like a predator in pursuit of terrified prey. Then, with just one shot from its high-caliber cannon, it turns its prey into a steaming smear of blood on a hot slab of desert stone.

With its reserves of active boots on the ground, Militech's leadership believed it was always burning money and resources on the same old problems. Soldiers have to be trained. They have to be equipped, fed and paid. Then, after absorbing all that capital, one quick bullet to the head is enough to send the investment straight down the drain. As a result, Militech executives salivated at the prospect of using machines to replace a portion of their unreliable, "soft" human assets. Thus, the Griffin combat drone was born. Cheap, obedient and durable, the Griffin never posed a risk of desertion or demanded a pay raise. And if one ever committed a war crime? Militech could blame it on a "software bug" caused by a sloppy third-party contractor. Managing an army had never been easier.

Night City's police have complained to their superiors for decades that their lives are in constant danger. They fight criminals who are equipped with combat cyberware, high-caliber weapons, high-grade explosives and military hardware traded on the black market. Each officer suits up for work every day never knowing if they'll be the next badge-wearing fly splattered against a wall.\n\nThe issue of officer safety is often revisted between NCPD leadership and city politicians. Every now and again, a plucky, young aide to a city councilmember suggests that the city implement stricter gun control measures. Once the laughter in the room subsides, the meetings typically conclude with the city commissioning Militech for a new fleet of Manticores, their line of armored AVs designed for military operations. Everyone walks away pleased. The NCPD gets fancy new toys, the City Council announces another public safety success, Militech pockets another billion-eurodollar arms deal, and they all live happily ever after (until the next year).

In the second half of the 21st century, business is a battlefield – both figuratively and literally. Arbitration, lawsuits, settlements – these measures carry less weight in a world where corporate disputes are often fast-tracked to resolution through sabotage and assassination. For the prudent corporate employee, it's wise to arrive at any arranged business meeting in a suit made from reinforced polymers with a pistol tucked in the belt. Even then, most expect that the other side likely hasn't shown up empty-handed either; such naivete is often enough to get you killed. For those businesspeople seeking an edge in negotiations, Militech offers the Wyvern drone. When deactivated, it fits conveniently into a briefcase which can be concealed easily under a limo seat or in the corner of a conference room. When activated, it can turn a stubborn business partner into an obedient lapdog... or a bloody heap on the floor.

Rayfield is renown the world over for their exclusive and luxurious hypercars: the Caliburn and the Aerondight. But even expensive cars suffer from the same, age-old problem as any other on the road: they can get caught in traffic. Sure, you could ask your security detail to empty a clip at the drivers ahead, subtly urging them to kindly get out of your way; however, most Rayfield owners prefer to avoid such inelegant behavior. To circumvent the burden of traffic altogether for their illustrious clientele, Rayfield engineered the Excalibur, a luxury AV that allows you to travel punctually, safely and – most importantly – in maximum comfort and style. That is, assuming your bank account is as close to bottomless as possible.

The Larimore is a variation on the popular Thorton Mackinaw, differing only in the fact that the truck bed is covered. This truck is an excellent choice for anyone transporting expensive or delicate goods (e.g. fresh produce) or anyone concealing something best left unseen by NCPD patrol cars and AVs (e.g. drugs and bodies). And for the auto owner down on their luck, the Larimore works as the perfect house on wheels. It can fit a mattress, a mobile feeder-entertainment unit and even a mini fridge in the back with no sacrifice to your privacy other than the occasional routine vehicle search. What more could you ask for?

The Atlus is the flagship product of Zetatech and probably the most popular AV model in Night City, used by both Trauma Team medic squads and N54 News teams. Its characteristic hum can be heard day and night in any district or neighborhood. When parents ask their toddlers what sound an Atlus makes, the little rug rats reply "Woom woom!" as they point up to the smoggy sky.\n\nWhat made the Atlus so successful? The sleek design, attractive price tag and dependable performance helped to be sure. But the most important factor was hiring Kieran Oesterlitz as Zetatech's chief lobbyist. Already on a first name basis with most of the city's bigwigs, Kieran knows that it's personal connections, not technical specs, that sell AVs.

The Bombus was designed as a caretaker drone because, as most would agree, who honestly has the time to raise children? You're back in the office the day after you give birth, working twelve, thirteen, fourteen hours, then another three stuck in traffic. Make dinner? Change a diaper? No chance in hell!

Fortunately, the Bombus can fill the role of the dutiful parent: watching over the kids, playing hide-and-seek and popping scop dogs in the microwave. And if your child catches a stray bullet through the window, no problem! The Bombus will even call for an ambulance!

Unsurpisingly, with its simple and inexpensive design, the Bombus has found applications in other sectors as well. Courier services use them for deliveries, the NCPD uses them for reconnaissance and gangs duct tape explosives to them to make remote-controlled bombs. Is there no problem a Bombus can't solve?

The Canopy is Zetatech's response to the Aras waste-collection drone from the Soviet-owned Kaukaz corporation. Unlike the Aras, the Canopy was designed with the American market in mind, making it better suited to local demands. For example, its sensors and collection measures are better equipped to handle upwards of a thousand of XXXXXL-size soda cups when compared to the Aras.\n\nA long time ago, parents used to tell their unruly children to behave and focus on their schoolwork or they would wind up sweeping the streets for a living. Well, with the Canopy hard at work, now even that safety net is long gone.

Until recently, most considered Zetatech a second-rate company, living in the shadow of giants like Araska and Militech. But today, those same people will now admit Zetatech has proven its mettle in manufacturing products that match the quality of their megacorp rivals and are even sold at a lower price.\n\nTake, for example, the Octant. Sure, maybe it lacks the elegance characteristic of Arasaka, maybe its composite materials aren't as high-grade as Militech's, but when it comes down to sheer firepower, the Octant is second to none. This drone series has quickly emerged as a favorite for dictators around the world who aim to pacify mass protests and wipe resistance cells off the map. When Zetatech sold its thousandth Octant, champagne bottles were popped throughout the company's corporate offices. They achieved a sales milestone they could truly be proud of.

From the day the first flying car was made, experts were already making their predictions about the first flying bus and who would produce it. In the end, it was Zetatech who won the flying bus race when they released the Surveyor. This behemoth of the heavens is capable of delivering a platoon of troops behind enemy lines swiftly and silently. And although it was engineered primarily with personnel transportation in mind, the Surveyor is fitted with Smart-missile defense systems powerful enough to dependably fend off enemy attacks.\n\nInitially designed and sold for military applications, this colossal AV is now frequently used for civilian purposes in many large cities, including Night City. So when a sunny day quickly turns to night, just look up – it won't be a solar eclipse, but a Zetatech Surveyor.

Produced early in the 21st century, the Valgus was Zetatech's first combat helicopter. At the time, the company was still small and largely unknown, but, in retrospect, the achievement of the Valgus would serve as a litmus test for Zetatech's future success. Despite relatively poor top speeds and maneuverability, this machine has consistently proved to be reliable, even in hazardous weather conditions and climates. Whether in sweltering heat or biting frost, whenever the Valgus takes to the air, it puts suspicious targets into the ground.\n\nAlthough outdated by today's technological standards and outmatched by contemporary combat helicopters, the Valgus still finds use in both Militech and Arasaka fleets as well as along the North California-South California border. With a favorable price-to-performance ratio and low malfunction rate, this model will continue to patrol the skies and gun down unarmed immigrants for quite some time.

Shit, V. Even the two of us put together aren't as fucked in the head as this guy. Sorry, MAN. I mean, fuck the cave shit, just look at those manifestos on justice in this town. Choom really thinks Night City can be saved. Still, whatever our murky friend's missing in the sanity department, he makes up for with his excellent taste in fine automobiles. And hey – he's not the only one who loves a good ride, am I right?

A photo shoot in Wraith territory? Respect. Nothing sells like a good 'n' gory firefight. Man, if you'd seen our ultra underground word-of-mouth gigs... Anyway, looks like they were trying to sell some fucking overpriced sadrags, but at least some choom had the corpoballs to drag 'em all out here in that sweet, sweet ride.
